title: Conserva di Rose (Rose Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with rose petals, lemon, and sugar.
steps: Place the roses in a bowl with 200 grams of the sugar and the juice of half a lemon and with your hands rub them, chop them as much as possible to reduce them to nearly a paste.

Dissolve the rest of the sugar in the water over the fire and add the roses to it to boil until the syrup is condensed, which is known if, taking a drop between the fingers, it begins to stick; but be careful that it does not reach the thread stage.
Before removing them from the fire, give them color with breton, which you can omit if you do not care about the beautiful color.
When the preserve is cooled, put it in small jars to preserve it like all the other similar ones.

title: Conserva di Susine (Plum Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with plums and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: Plums, preferably Claudia variety, any quantity
ingredients.sourceText: Plums, preferably Claudia variety, any quantity

ingredients.name: White powdered sugar, 60 grams per 100 grams of fresh plums
ingredients.sourceText: White powdered sugar, 60 grams per 100 grams of fresh plums

steps: Remove the pits from the plums.
Boil for a few minutes.
Pass through a sieve.
Return to the heat with white powdered sugar in the proportion of 60 grams of sugar per 100 grams of fresh plums.
If mold forms after some time, it indicates insufficient cooking; remedy by returning to the heat.

title: Conserva Dolce di Pomodoro (Sweet Tomato Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with tomatoes, white sugar, and juice.
steps: The tomatoes for this use must be very ripe, pulpy, and possibly round.
Place them in very hot water so they can be peeled easily. After peeling, cut them in half and with the handle of a teaspoon remove the seeds.
Dissolve the sugar in the fire in two fingers (of a glass) of water, then throw in the tomatoes, the juice of the lemon, and a little of its grated skin.
During boiling over low heat in an uncovered pan, stir somewhat, and if any seeds appear that have remained, remove them.
Finally give it flavor with vanillated sugar and remove it when it has reached the consistency of common preserves.
Note: It is difficult to specify the quantity of sugar in this preserve, as it depends on how watery the tomatoes are. Make double the dose as it reduces greatly.

title: Cosciotto di Castrato Arrosto (Roasted Leg of Mutton)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, broth, and salt.
steps: Let it age for several days before cooking, more or less depending on temperature.
Beat it well with a wooden mallet before threading onto the spit.
Skin it and remove the middle bone without damaging it too much.
Tie it so it stays compact and apply intense heat at first, then reduce heat halfway through cooking.
When it begins to release juices, collect them in the dripping pan and baste with the same juices and degreased broth, nothing else.
Salt when cooking is almost complete; ensure it is not overcooked nor bloody.
Serve at table with its juices in a sauceboat and wrap the end of the leg bone in fringed white paper for better presentation.

title: Cosciotto o Spalla di Castrato in Cazzaruola I (Braised Mutton Leg or Shoulder I)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, rind, and onion.

ingredients.name: shoulder or leg of mutton, boned
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kg shoulder or leg of mutton, boned

ingredients.name: Strips of lardoon or prosciutto rind
ingredients.sourceText: Strips of lardoon or prosciutto rind

ingredients.name: 1 bunch tied together of parsley, celery and carrot
ingredients.sourceText: 1 bunch tied together of parsley, celery and carrot

ingredients.name: Broken bones from the shoulder or leg
ingredients.sourceText: Broken bones from the shoulder or leg

ingredients.name: 1 glass of broth or half a glass
ingredients.sourceText: 1 glass of broth or half a glass

ingredients.name: Cold water to nearly cover the meat
ingredients.sourceText: Cold water to nearly cover the meat

steps: Bone the shoulder and lard it with lardoon strips
Season inside and out with salt and pepper
Roll it up and tie it to achieve a nice shape
Place it in a braising pan with 40 grams of butter to brown it
Add the lardoon or prosciutto rinds, the tied bunch of herbs, the whole onion, the broken bones, meat scraps if you have them, the glass of broth or half a glass, and 2 or 3 tablespoons of brandy
Add enough cold water so the liquid reaches just below the surface of the mutton
Cover the pan well and simmer slowly until the meat is cooked, which will take four or more hours if the animal is tough
Strain the sauce, degrease it and discard the excess
Serve the mutton, optionally garnished with carrots, turnips, or beans prepared according to the instructions given in the text

description: Prepared with mutton, onion, and water or broth.

steps: Bone the shoulder and lard it with lardoon strips wrapped in salt and pepper
Salt it somewhat
Roll it up and tie it tightly
Place it on the fire with 40 grams of butter and the half onion studded with a clove to take on color
Remove the braising pan from the fire and pour in a glass of water or better broth, {{source-6}}, an aromatic bunch, and if it is tomato season, some tomatoes broken up
Boil gently for about three hours with the pan covered with double sheets of paper, turning the meat frequently
When cooked, discard the onion, strain the sauce, degrease it and add it to the meat when serving
Do not cook it too much or it will not be able to be cut into slices

title: Coteghino Fasciato (Wrapped Coteghino)
description: Prepared with veal or beef, celery, and carrot.

ingredients.name: Coteghino weighing about 300 grams, skinned raw
ingredients.sourceText: Coteghino weighing about 300 grams, skinned raw

ingredients.name: Lean veal or beef slice, 200 to 300 grams, wide and thin
ingredients.sourceText: Lean veal or beef slice, 200 to 300 grams, wide and thin

steps: Skin the coteghino raw and beat the veal or beef slice well
Wrap the coteghino with the meat slice, tie it all with string and put it on the fire in a pot with a piece of butter, celery, carrot and a quarter onion, all cut coarsely
When the piece has taken color on all sides, pour in enough water to cover it halfway and add some pieces of dried mushrooms, letting it boil slowly until completely cooked
Pass the gravy, unite the mushrooms to it and use this with cheese and butter to dress pasta, serving the wrapped coteghino, freed from the string, with some of its gravy around it as accompaniment
To thicken the gravy for the pasta, put a pinch of flour in a pot with a piece of butter and when it begins to take color pour the gravy into it and let it boil a little
The contorno of carrots works well with this dish, first boiled to two-thirds done, then finished in that gravy

title: Cotognata (Quince Paste)
description: Prepared with quinces and white sugar.
steps: Put the quinces on the fire covered with water and when they begin to crack, remove them, peel them and scrape them as best you can to remove all the pulp, then pass it through a sieve.
Put it back on the fire with the sugar and stir it constantly so it doesn't stick.
Seven or eight minutes of boiling will be enough; but then, if taken up with a spoon it begins to fall in shreds, remove it.

If you put it in vessels it can serve you as a preserve and made this way it will remain whiter than the one I will describe at No. 741, but with less fragrance, because part of the particular odor of this fruit is lost in the water.
To reduce it to quince paste, spread it on a board about the thickness of a coin and dry it in the sun covered with a veil because flies and wasps are very fond of it.
When it is dry on top, cut it in the form of chocolate tablets and by passing a knife under it to detach it from the board, turn it over on the opposite side.

If you would like to give it bizarre forms, procure some tin molds empty on both sides, fill them, smooth them and detaching the marmalade from the edges carefully, place it equally on the board and dry it in the same manner.

You can also coat it with sugar if you wish, and then put 100 grams of white sugar to melt with two spoonfuls of water and when it has boiled enough to form a thread (taking a drop between two fingers) spread each piece with a brush.
If the sugar hardens during the operation (which is best to do on a not humid day) put it back on the fire with another drop of water and boil it again.
When the sugar is dry on one side and on the edges, spread the opposite side.

title: Cotolette di Baccalà (Salt Cod Cutlets)
description: Prepared with salt, anchovies, and parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: bread crumb paste (made from bread marrow, water, and butter), 3-4 spoonfuls
ingredients.sourceText: bread crumb paste (made from bread marrow, water, and butter), 3-4 spoonfuls

ingredients.name: lemon, cut into wedges or tomato sauce
ingredients.sourceText: lemon, cut into wedges or tomato sauce

steps: Boil the salt cod as in the preceding recipe.
Finely chop the anchovies, parsley, and salt cod together with a knife.
Add pepper, grated Parmesan, and the bread crumb paste made from bread marrow, water, and butter to make it more tender, along with two eggs.
Form the mixture into spoonfuls and dip each into breadcrumbs.
Flatten with your hands to give them the shape of cutlets.
Dip the cutlets into beaten egg and then coat again in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil and serve with lemon wedges or tomato sauce.
Half this quantity will make 9 or 10 cutlets.

title: Cotolette di Carciofi (Artichoke Cutlets)
description: Prepared with artichokes, parmesan cheese, and egg yolk.
steps: Take two large artichokes, clean them of hard leaves and scrape the stem, then boil them, but not too much, and while still boiling cut them lengthwise into five slices each, leaving some stem, and season with salt and pepper.
Make a béchamel sauce: melt the butter, add the flour, and gradually add the milk, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and mix in an egg yolk, the Parmesan, and a pinch of salt.

Taking them up one by one by the stem, dip the artichoke slices in the béchamel, lay them on a tray and cover them with the remaining béchamel using a spoon. After several hours, when they are completely cold, coat them with a beaten egg, bread them, and fry them in oil or lard.

title: Cotolette Imbottite (Stuffed Cutlets)
description: Prepared with veal or chicken or turkey breast, parmesan cheese, and egg yolk.

ingredients.name: veal or chicken or turkey breast, trimmed of bone
ingredients.sourceText: 170 grams veal or chicken or turkey breast, trimmed of bone

steps: Lightly fry the thin cutlets in butter, salt them, and set aside.
Make a béchamel sauce with the flour, butter, and milk. Once removed from heat, salt it, add the parmesan cheese and egg yolk, mixing well.
Once the béchamel has cooled, spread it on both sides of the cutlets to the thickness of a coin, evening it out with a knife blade dipped in oil.
Dip the cutlets in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs, and fry them in oil or lard until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Crema Fritta I (Fried Cream)
description: Prepared with cornstarch, sugar, and butter.
steps: Work the eggs with the sugar, then add the cornstarch reduced to powder, the grated lemon zest, the milk poured little by little and the butter.

Put the mixture on the fire stirring continuously as you would for a common cream and when it is condensed so that it no longer grows, add the pinch of salt and pour it onto a tray or board, spreading it to the thickness of a finger.
Cut it into almond shapes when it is well cold, coat it with egg and breadcrumbs, fry it in lard or oil and serve it hot as a side dish to other fried foods.

description: Prepared with sweetbreads, onion or butter or gravy, and béchamel.

ingredients.sourceText: optional: fat and lean ham, salted tongue, truffles

title: Crostini di capperi (Capers Crostini)
description: Prepared with capers, powdered sugar, and raisins.

ingredients.name: Bread slices, fried in good oil or lightly toasted
ingredients.sourceText: Bread slices, fried in good oil or lightly toasted

steps: Chop the capers coarsely
Clean the raisins of stems and wash them well
Cut the pine nuts into three parts lengthwise
Shape the prosciutto into very small dice and reduce the candied fruit into small pieces

Put a heaping teaspoon of flour and two teaspoons of sugar in a small saucepan over the fire; when this mixture has taken on a brown color, pour in half a glass of water mixed with a small amount of vinegar

When it has boiled until the lumps dissolve, throw all the ingredients into the saucepan at once and let them boil for ten minutes, tasting them meanwhile to feel if the sweet and strong flavor is right
When the mixture is still hot, spread it over thin slices of bread fried in good oil or simply lightly toasted
Serve these crostini cold, or in the middle of the meal to excite the appetite of your guests

title: Crostini di fegatini di pollo (Chicken Liver Crostini)
description: Prepared with chicken, shallot or onion, and fat.

ingredients.name: One shallot or one small white onion bulb
ingredients.sourceText: One shallot or one small white onion bulb

steps: Remove the bile sac from the chicken livers carefully without breaking it, doing this best while working in a bowl of water

Place the livers on the fire together with a mixture (battutino) composed of one shallot or, if unavailable, one small white onion bulb, a piece of prosciutto fat, several parsley leaves, celery and carrot, a little oil and butter, salt and pepper; but everything in small quantity so as not to make the mixture piquant or nauseating
At half cooking, remove the livers and dry them; with two or three pieces of softened dried mushrooms, mince them finely with a crescent-shaped chopper
Return them to the fire in the sauce that remained from the half-cooking and with a little broth finish cooking them
Before serving, bind them with a pinch of fine breadcrumbs and add a bit of lemon juice
The crostini should be tender, so make the mixture somewhat liquid, or dip the bread slices briefly, barely, in the broth

title: Crostini di fegatini di pollo con la salvia (Chicken Liver Crostini with Sage)
description: Prepared with chicken, sage, and onion.

ingredients.name: Bread, stale crumb, slices about 1 centimeter thick
ingredients.sourceText: Bread, stale crumb, slices about 1 centimeter thick

steps: Make a mixture (battutino) with very little onion and both fat and lean prosciutto
Put it on the fire with a piece of butter and when it is well browned, throw in the finely minced chicken livers together with sage leaves (4 or 5 for 3 livers should be enough)
Season with salt and pepper and, once they have released their moisture, add another piece of butter and bind them with a teaspoon of flour
Wet them with broth to cook them
Before removing from the fire, pour in 3 or 4 teaspoons of grated Parmesan and taste to see if the seasoning is right
Form the crostini from the crumb of stale bread, just under 1 centimeter thick, and spread them generously on one side only with the mixture when it is no longer boiling

After several hours, when you are about to serve them, either alone or as a side to roasted meat, beat an egg mixed with a drop of water and, taking the crostini one by one, let them touch the flour from the side of the mixture only, then immerse them in the egg and throw them into the pan on the mixture side

title: Crostini di Tre Colori (Three-Color Croutons)
description: Prepared with spinach or juice or butter, butter or oil, and eggs.

ingredients.name: spinach, cooked with juice or butter and parmesan
ingredients.sourceText: spinach, cooked with juice or butter and parmesan

steps: Cut the two chifels into thick slices one centimeter wide and fry them in butter or oil.
Take spinach cooked with juice or butter and parmesan, finely chopped, and cover the slices of chifel with a layer of the same.
Take two hard-boiled eggs, shell them, cut them in half crosswise and set aside the yolks.
From the white cut many concentric circles and place them over the layer of spinach.
From the yolk make many small pieces or small dice and place them in the middle of the circles of white.

In this way you will form croutons that can surround a roast dish which, having as a base fried bread covered by the green of the spinach, with the white and the yellow-red of the eggs will appear in three colors.

title: Cuscussù (Couscous)
description: Prepared with veal, semolina, and chicken liver.

ingredients.name: Vegetables of various kinds such as onion, savoy cabbage, celery, carrot, spinach, beet or other
ingredients.sourceText: Vegetables of various kinds such as onion, savoy cabbage, celery, carrot, spinach, beet or other

ingredients.name: Meat broth or tomato sauce or tomato conserve
ingredients.sourceText: Meat broth or tomato sauce or tomato conserve

steps: Put the semolina in a flat wide earthenware vessel or in a tinned copper pan, season it with a pinch of salt and a dash of pepper and, pouring over it drop by drop two fingers' worth (of a glass) scant of water, knead it with the palm of your hand to make it swell, become granular and loose.
When the water is finished, pour over it, little by little, a spoonful of oil and continue manipulating it in the same manner, lasting between the first and second operation more than half an hour.
Having conditioned the semolina in this way, put it in a soup bowl and cover it with a cloth, the excess of which, passing it underneath, you will tie tightly with twine.

Put the veal breast on the fire with three liters of water to make broth and after skimming the pot, cover its mouth with the bowl already prepared, so that the broth remains at some distance; but make sure that the mouths of the two vessels fit together and do not let smoke escape.
Leave the semolina thus for an hour and a quarter so it has time to cook by steam, open the wrapping halfway through cooking to mix it and then put it back as before.

Chop with a knife the 150 grams of lean meat, add to it a piece of bread marrow crumbled, season it with salt and pepper, make many small meatballs slightly larger than a hazelnut and fry them in oil.

Chop the vegetables somewhat and put first the onion to soften in oil and when it has taken color throw down the others, season them with salt and pepper, stir often and let them draw out the water they release.
Reduced almost to dryness, moisten them with meat juice, or with broth and tomato juice or conserve, to bring them to cooking together with the chicken liver cut into pieces and with the meatballs.

Remove the semolina from the wrapping, put it on the fire in a saucepan and without letting it boil dissolve into it the egg yolk, pour into it part of the said sauce, mix and pour it into a serving dish, but almost dry so it presents fullness, which you will decorate with the hard-boiled egg cut into small wedges.

Mix the rest of the sauce into the broth in the pot and send this broth to table divided into as many cups as there are diners, accompanied, of course, by the serving dish of semolina; thus each one draws down into his plate a portion of semolina and drinks after it the broth by spoonfuls.
The veal breast is served afterward as boiled meat.

title: Dolce di Mandorle (Almond Cake)
description: A cake made with potato flour, sweet almonds, and eggs.

ingredients.name: Sugar, equal weight to the eggs
ingredients.sourceText: Sugar, equal weight to the eggs

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with three bitter ones, 125 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Sweet almonds with three bitter ones, 125 grams

steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the sun or by the fire and pound them very finely in a mortar with a third of the said sugar
Work with a wooden spoon the three egg yolks with the remaining sugar and the lemon zest until they become whitish
Add the potato flour, then the pounded almonds and the melted butter, working the mixture further
Lastly add the beaten egg whites and when everything is amalgamated together, bake it in the oven
Dust it with powdered sugar while still hot
Use a baking pan with a bottom diameter of approximately 22 centimeters for proper height
You can use the same butter to grease the pan, which, as you know, should be dusted with powdered sugar mixed with flour

title: Dolce Roma (Roman Sweet)
description: Prepared with apples, wine, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: Apples of fine quality, not too ripe and medium-sized, 600 grams (5 or 6 apples)
ingredients.sourceText: Apples of fine quality, not too ripe and medium-sized, 600 grams (5 or 6 apples)

steps: Choose fine apples that are not too ripe and of medium size, weighing about 600 grams.
Remove the cores with a tin tube and peel them.
Place them to cook with 2 deciliters of white alcoholic wine and 130 grams of sugar, taking care that they do not break while boiling, turning them, and that they do not overcook.
Remove them dried and place them with the hole vertical in a decent vessel that can be brought to the table and that withstands fire.
Prepare a cream with 4 deciliters of milk, 3 egg yolks, 70 grams of sugar, 20 grams of flour and vanilla sugar flavoring, then pour it over the apples.
Whip the three remaining egg whites, and when they are well stiff add 20 grams of powdered sugar and cover the cream with them.
Place the sweet in a country oven or only on the hearth with just its cover, with fire above and little below to brown the surface.
Before sending it to the table, brush it with the reduced syrup remaining from the cooking of the apples.
This will suffice for seven or eight people.

title: Dolce Torino (Turin Sweet)
description: Prepared with chocolate, powdered sugar, and egg yolk.
steps: Cut the savoiardi in half lengthwise and soak them with rosolio, or better, half with rosolio and half with alkermes, so they can be alternated to make a better appearance.
First work the butter with the sugar and egg yolk.
Place the chocolate, grated or in pieces, on the fire with the milk, and when it is well dissolved pour it hot into the worked butter, add the flavoring and form thus a paste by mixing it well.
Arrange on the platter a first layer of the said savoiardi and spread them lightly with the said paste; then layer another layer of savoiardi, then a third layer still, always spreading them lightly.
Pour all the remaining paste over and at the sides, evening it out as well as you can.

The next day, before serving it, smooth it all over the surface with the blade of a knife heated by fire, and at the same time, if you like, decorate it with a sprinkling of pistachios or slightly toasted hazelnuts, both finely chopped.
40 grams of hazelnuts weighed with shell or 15 grams of pistachios will suffice.
This is a portion for six or seven people.

description: A pastry dish made with white wine, flour, and oil.

ingredients.name: White wine or Marsala, two spoonfuls
ingredients.sourceText: White wine or Marsala, two spoonfuls

title: Fagiuolini con l'odore di vaniglia (Green Beans with Vanilla Scent)
description: Prepared with green beans, vanilla, and shallot.
steps: Soak the green beans in fresh water
If they are tender, put them whole and raw into a stew without draining them too much
Make a soffritto with oil, shallot, parsley, carrot and celery, all finely chopped

Throw in the green beans to cook them
Before removing them from heat, season with two teaspoons of vanilla sugar
If this flavor is not pleasing, substitute with nepitella

title: Fagiuolini in salsa d'uovo (Green Beans in Egg Sauce)
description: A sauce made with green beans, egg yolk, and juice.
steps: Remove both ends and the string from the green beans
Blanch them in salted water until half-cooked
Drain and cut into three pieces
Sauté with butter, salt and pepper to taste
Whisk together the egg yolk, flour, and lemon juice in a pot
Dilute the mixture with one ladle of degreased cold broth
Place over heat, stirring constantly with a spoon, until it becomes a flowing cream
Pour the sauce over the green beans
Keep them on the heat a little longer so the sauce incorporates well
Serve as a side dish to boiled meat

title: Farinata Gialla di Magro (Yellow Cornmeal Polenta Lean Style)
description: Prepared with cornmeal, white beans, and cabbage.

ingredients.name: Half a head of white or savoy cabbage, chopped
ingredients.sourceText: Half a head of white or savoy cabbage, chopped

ingredients.name: Two cloves of garlic, whole and peeled
ingredients.sourceText: Two cloves of garlic, whole and peeled

ingredients.name: Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water
ingredients.sourceText: Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water

steps: Put the beans on the fire with proportioned water.

After they are cooked, pass them through a sieve and mix the paste in the broth of the same beans and in the same put to boil, for about two hours, the chopped cabbage which you will season with salt, pepper and thyme leaves.

Put a pan on the fire with oil in good measure and two whole peeled cloves of garlic; when these are well browned throw them away and add to the oil tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water and also here another little salt and pepper.
When it has boiled somewhat, pour also this seasoning into the pot where the broth and cabbage are.

Finally, when this is cooked, pour with one hand, little by little, the cornmeal flour; with the other hand mix well, so that lumps do not form, and when it has reached a certain consistency, that is somewhat liquid, let it boil a little more and serve it.

title: Fegato alla Cacciatora (Hunter-Style Liver)
description: Prepared with liver, onions, and lard.

ingredients.name: good red wine, less than half a glass
ingredients.sourceText: good red wine, less than half a glass

steps: Slice three large onions and soak them in fresh water for one or two hours.
Drain the water and put the onion in a pan to dry it; once dry, add the lard to fry it.
When it has taken on a brown color, add the liver cut into thin slices.
Let it soften somewhat, mixed with the onion; then pour less than half a glass of good red wine into the pan.
After five minutes, stirring constantly, serve it seasoned with salt and pepper.
Note that this is not a dish for delicate stomachs.

steps: First work the egg yolks with the sugar, add the flour, then the almonds peeled and pounded fine with a spoonful of the said sugar.

title: Folaghe in Umido (Braised Coots)
description: Prepared with onion, celery, and carrot.

ingredients.name: 3 eggs of pappardelle or 500 grams strips
ingredients.sourceText: 3 eggs of pappardelle or 500 grams strips

steps: After plucking the coots and singing them by flame to remove the down, gut them and wash them well.

Pierce them lengthwise through the body with a hot spit, then cut them into four parts throwing away the head, feet and wing tips; then keep them soaking in vinegar for an hour and afterward wash them several times in fresh water.
Do the same with the gizzards after emptying, washing and cutting them into four pieces.

Make a finely chopped mixture with a large onion and all the herbs in proportion, that is celery, carrot and parsley, and put it on the fire with 80 grams of butter, and at the same time the coots and gizzards seasoning them with salt, pepper and spice flavor.
When they are dry bathe them with tomato sauce or paste dissolved in abundant water to cook them and so that much sauce remains.

Once cooked, strain the sauce and into it add a coot breast and a half finely chopped and another 40 grams of butter, to season with it and with Parmigiano cheese three eggs of pappardelle or 500 grams of strips which, for their particular taste, will be praised.
Serve the coots with some of their sauce afterward as a main dish that will not be despised.
This entire preparation should be enough for five or six persons.

title: Fricandò (Braised Veal with Vegetables)
description: Prepared with fat, onion, and carrot.

ingredients.name: A piece of milk-fed veal from the thigh, all in one piece
ingredients.sourceText: A piece of milk-fed veal from the thigh, all in one piece

ingredients.name: Fat and lean prosciutto for larding
ingredients.sourceText: Fat and lean prosciutto for larding

steps: Lard the veal with prosciutto.
Tie the piece and salt it sparingly or not at all because oversalting is the worst defect in food.
Stud an onion with two cloves and make a bouquet with carrot cut into strips, celery and parsley.
Put everything in a pot with a piece of butter, brown the meat and cook it through with broth.
When cooked, discard the onion and bouquet, strain the sauce, remove the fat and reduce it separately until it becomes a jelly that you will add to the fricandò when you serve it at table.

title: Fricassea (Veal Fricassee)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, lemon, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Flour, 5 grams or one scant tablespoon
ingredients.sourceText: Flour, 5 grams or one scant tablespoon

ingredients.name: Salt and white pepper to taste
ingredients.sourceText: Salt and white pepper to taste

ingredients.name: Fresh mushrooms, 100 to 150 grams (if in season), or a pinch of dried mushrooms
ingredients.sourceText: Fresh mushrooms, 100 to 150 grams (if in season), or a pinch of dried mushrooms

steps: Cut the breast into pieces leaving all the bones.
Put a pot on the fire with half the butter and when it begins to melt, pour in the flour stirring until it takes on a hazel color.

Then begin to pour the water little by little and then the bouquet which you can compose of some strips of onion and carrot, threads of parsley, celery and basil, all tied together, excluding the leaves because these could fall apart and spoil the fricassee, one of whose merits is to have a beautiful straw color.
When the water boils throw in the meat and the rest of the butter and season with salt and white pepper, which is the finest pepper.
Cover the pot with a sheet of paper held firm by the lid and let it boil slowly.
At two-thirds cooking time remove the bouquet and, if it is mushroom season, you can make it more agreeable with 100 or 150 grams of these cut into thin slices; if not, a pinch of dried mushrooms.
When ready to serve, remove the pot from the fire and pour in little by little, stirring, the egg yolks whisked with lemon juice.

title: Frittata in Riccioli per Contorno (Curled Omelette Strips as Garnish)
description: Prepared with spinach, parmesan cheese, and eggs.
steps: Boil a bunch of spinach and pass it through a sieve
Beat two eggs, season with salt and pepper, and mix in the spinach in such quantity as to make them only green
Put a pan on the fire with just a drop of oil to grease it, and when very hot pour in a portion of the egg mixture, turning the pan in every direction so the omelette comes out thin as paper
When well set and dry, remove it, flipping if necessary, and repeat or triple the operation with the remaining eggs
Roll these two or three omelettes together, cut them into fine strips like noodles, and lightly fry them in butter
Season with Parmesan and use these strips as a garnish for fricandeau or similar dishes

title: Frittelle di Polenta alla Lodigiana (Fried Polenta Cakes, Lodi Style)
description: A cake made with cheese, breadcrumbs, and lard or oil.
steps: Make a polenta from the milk and cornmeal and before removing it from the fire, salt it
While boiling pour it onto a work surface and with a table knife dipped in water spread it to a thickness of slightly less than half a finger
When cold, using a stamp cutter of recipe N. 182 or similar, cut as many disks as will yield 30 or 32 if you add the scraps by kneading and flattening them with your hands
Pair these disks by putting a slice of Gruyère between them, obtaining thus 15 to 16 frittelle
Beat two eggs, which are necessary to be able to gild them with these and with breadcrumbs, and fry them in lard or oil
Serve them hot as a side dish to a roast

Dust them as usual with powdered sugar and serve them hot.

title: Fritto alla Garisenda (Fried Sandwich, Garisenda Style)
description: Prepared with bread, fat, and truffle.

ingredients.name: slices of prosciutto, fat and lean
ingredients.sourceText: slices of prosciutto, fat and lean

steps: Remove the crust from stale bread and cut it into almond shapes or squares of about four centimeters per side, all of equal size.
On each piece lay first a slice of prosciutto, then slices of truffle, and on top a slice of Gruyère cheese.
Cover the filling with matching pieces of bread, pressing them together to hold them in place. Cut all components thin so the fried pieces are not too large.
Lightly moisten with cold milk and once it is absorbed, dip each piece in beaten egg, then in breadcrumbs, repeating the egg and breadcrumb coating twice so the edges are also golden and sealed.
Fry in lard or oil and serve alone or mixed with other fried dishes.

title: Gelatina (Aspic Jelly)
description: Prepared with meat, calf's foot, and chickens.

ingredients.name: One calf's foot or 150 grams of calf's foot
ingredients.sourceText: One calf's foot or 150 grams of calf's foot

ingredients.name: Feet of two or three chickens
ingredients.sourceText: Feet of two or three chickens

ingredients.name: Two chicken heads with their necks
ingredients.sourceText: Two chicken heads with their necks

ingredients.name: A finger's width (of glass) of water
ingredients.sourceText: A finger's width (of glass) of water

steps: Singe the chicken feet over fire and cut them into pieces
Put everything into a pot with two liters of cold water
Salt sufficiently and boil, skimming, slowly for seven or eight continuous hours so that the liquid reduces by half
Pour the broth into a basin and when it has set, remove the fat from the surface
If it does not congeal, return it to the fire to reduce further, or add two sheets of fish glue
To clarify and give it amber color, finely mince 70 grams of lean veal meat with a knife and then pound it in a mortar
Place it in a small pot with one egg and a finger's width of water, mix everything well and pour in the cold aspic jelly
Do not stop beating it with a whisk over the fire until it rises to a boil, then boil slowly for about twenty minutes, during which taste to check the salt and give it color

For the color, place two pinches of sugar and a drop of water in a non-tinned metal spoon, hold it over fire until the sugar becomes almost black, pouring it little by little into the boiling aspic jelly to achieve the correct color gradation
Take a towel, wet it in water, wring it well and pass the warm aspic jelly through it without squeezing, and pour it immediately into molds
In summer, if it does not set well, place the molds on ice
When you wish to unmold it, pass a cloth dipped in boiling water lightly around the molds

title: Gelatina di Arancio in Gelo (Orange Gelatin in Ice)
description: Prepared with orange, isinglass, and rum.
steps: Soak the isinglass and, changing the water once, leave it for one or two hours.
Boil the sugar in half of the aforementioned water for ten minutes and strain it through a cloth.
Squeeze the orange and lemon into this syrup, passing their juice through the same cloth.
Take the isinglass that has been soaked and bring it to a boil in the remaining two deciliters of water and pour this also into the said syrup.
Add to it the alkermes and rum, mix everything and when it begins to cool pour it into the mold held in ice in summer and in cold water in winter.

description: Prepared with chocolate, milk, and sugar.
steps: Grate the chocolate and place it on the fire with the sugar and four deciliters of the aforementioned milk in a saucepan where it will remain confined.
Let it boil for a few minutes, stirring it constantly so that it refines.

title: Gelato di Torrone (Nougat Ice Cream)
description: Prepared with squash, citron, and almonds.
steps: Make a cream with the milk, the sugar and the egg yolks, giving it the flavor of vanilla, and pour it into the sorbetierre.
When it is frozen mix into it the aforementioned ingredients. Blanch the pistachios and almonds in hot water; divide those into three parts and mince these to the size of a vetch and toast them.
Cut the candied fruit into thin slices and the squash into small cubes, which being red will make a more beautiful appearance.
If the milk is good, by boiling it for half an hour with the sugar in it, you can do without the egg yolks, but the mixture will then be of less flavor.

The almonds in this and similar cases come out better toasted in the following manner. title: Germano in Umido II (Braised Mallard Duck II)
description: Prepared with duck, celery, and carrot.

ingredients.name: 1 celery rib about a palm long
ingredients.sourceText: 1 celery rib about a palm long

steps: Put the mallard duck in a pot with 30 grams of butter and let it brown.
Remove it and throw a tablespoon of flour into the remaining fat, stirring with a spoon until it takes on a brown color.

Remove from heat and not at a boil anymore, pour half a liter of water over that mixture and put the duck back in; season with salt and pepper and let it boil covered until completely cooked with a quarter of an orange peel in one piece, a celery rib about a palm long and a piece of carrot, both cut roughly.
Finally strain the sauce, break apart the duck at its joints, put it back in its sauce squeezing the juice of the orange over it to boil it a few more minutes and serve it.

title: Germano ossia Anatra Selvatica (Wild Duck)
description: Prepared with duck, fat, and celery.

ingredients.name: one wild duck (Anas boscas), about one kilogram
ingredients.sourceText: one wild duck (Anas boscas), about one kilogram

ingredients.name: prosciutto, fat and lean together
ingredients.sourceText: 30 grams of prosciutto, fat and lean together

ingredients.name: celery, parsley, carrot, one quarter of a large onion
ingredients.sourceText: celery, parsley, carrot, one quarter of a large onion

ingredients.name: black cabbage or whole lentils for accompaniment
ingredients.sourceText: black cabbage or whole lentils for accompaniment

steps: When you buy a wild duck in the market, open its beak to observe the tongue.
If you find it very dried out, you can say that the animal has been dead for a long time, and then smell it to make sure it does not stink.
Empty the duck, keeping the liver, heart and onion; remove its head and the skin of the neck, after having opened it to extract the vertebrae, fold it back over the animal's breast.
For a duck that weighs about one kilogram, finely chop {{source-1}}, with all the aromatics, that is celery, parsley, carrot and a quarter of a large onion.
Put everything together with oil in a casserole and on top of the mixture place the duck, seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Let it take on color from all sides and then add water to cook it through.

Cook the accompaniment of black cabbage or whole lentils in water and make it over in the aforementioned sauce: taste it to add, if necessary, a small piece of butter, which will make it more agreeable and flavorful, and combine it with the duck when you send it to the table.
Cut the cabbage coarsely and season it as well with salt and pepper.

description: Prepared with beef and salt.

Close the lid of the pot with several layers of paper held firm by the lid

It is almost better served cold than hot

title: Gnocchi (Gnocchi)
description: Prepared with potatoes, chicken, and cheese.

ingredients.name: Breast of chicken, boiled and finely minced, 40 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Breast of chicken, boiled and finely minced, 40 grams

steps: Cook 200 grams of large floury potatoes in water, or better by steam, and pass them through a sieve.
To these add the boiled chicken breast minced very finely with a crescent cutter, 40 grams of grated parmigiano, two egg yolks, salt to taste and a hint of nutmeg.
Mix and pour the mixture onto a work surface over 30 or 40 grams of flour to bind it and be able to pull it into sticks as thick as the little finger.
Cut these into small pieces and throw them into boiling broth where a cooking of five or six minutes will be sufficient.
This dose may be enough for seven or eight people.

title: Gâteau à la Noisette (Hazelnut Cake)
description: A cake made with rice flour, sweet almonds, and hazelnuts.
steps: Peel the hazelnuts with hot water as you would almonds, and dry both the hazelnuts and almonds well in the sun or by the fire. Then, after pounding them very finely, mix them with the rice flour using two tablespoons of the sugar.
Work the eggs well with the remaining sugar, then pour the almond and hazelnut mixture into it and stir very much with a whisk. Finally add the melted butter and work the mixture again.
Pour it into a smooth, rounded mold that is somewhat narrow so that it comes to a height of four or five fingers, and bake it in an oven at moderate heat. Serve it cold.
This amount will serve six or seven people.

title: Insalata Maionese (Mayonnaise Salad)
description: A salad made with lettuce, beets, and potatoes.

ingredients.name: anchovies, washed and cleaned of bones
ingredients.sourceText: anchovies, washed and cleaned of bones

steps: Take romaine lettuce or lettuce, cut it into strips one finger wide, mix with beets and boiled potatoes cut into thin slices, some washed anchovies, cleaned of the bone and cut into four or five parts, and finally boiled fish in small pieces.
You can add at most some capers and the flesh of two or three sweetened olives.
Season everything together with salt, oil and not too much vinegar, turn it over so it takes up the seasoning well and heap it all together so that it makes a mound.

Make a mayonnaise sauce as in recipe N. 126 which, in the dose indicated there, can be enough for seven or eight people; but instead of pepper give it the piquancy with a teaspoon of mustard and to the lemon add a drop of vinegar in which you can dissolve the mustard.

With this sauce spread all the salad on the surface and then decorate it with other slices of beets and potatoes alternated so that they make a fine show; if you have a suitable mold, place on top of the salad, for beauty, not to eat it, a flower made with butter.

title: Krapfen (Filled Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolk, chicken, and sweetbreads.

ingredients.name: Egg yolk, minced filling with gravy and béchamel
ingredients.sourceText: Egg yolk, minced filling with gravy and béchamel

steps: Mix the remaining ingredients with eggs, melted butter, sugar, and salt
If the dough is too soft, add enough flour so it can be rolled out to the thickness of half a finger
Cut discs using a tin circle of the designated size
Make 24 discs total
Using an egg or similar tool, press the point in the middle of each disc to make an indentation

On 12 of the discs, place a teaspoon of the filling made from minced liver, sweetbreads, prosciutto, salted tongue, flavored with truffles or mushrooms, all cut into small dice, combined with gravy and béchamel
Wet the edges of the discs with a finger dipped in water
Cover each filled disc with one of the remaining 12 empty discs
Press a tin circle of equal size on top to form an indentation all around
Let them rise with gentle heat, by the fire or in a stove
When well puffed, fry them in lard or oil until covered by the fat
Serve hot as a fried dish or intermediate course
For a sweet version, fill with firm cream or fruit preserve and dust with powdered sugar after cooking

title: Kugelhupf (Hungarian Yeast Cake)
description: A cake made with sultana, beer, and flour.

ingredients.name: Hungarian or very fine flour
ingredients.sourceText: 200 grams Hungarian or very fine flour

ingredients.name: one whole egg and two egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: one whole egg and two egg yolks

steps: Mix the yeast with warm milk and a handful of the said flour to form a rather firm small loaf; make a cross cut in it and place it in a small pan with a veil of milk underneath, covered and near the fire, making sure the fire does not heat it too much.
In winter, melt the butter in a water bath then work it somewhat with the whole egg, then pour in the sugar and then the flour, the egg yolks, the salt and the flavoring, mixing well.

Now add the yeast which in the meantime will have already swollen and with spoonfuls of warm milk, pour one at a time, work the mixture with a spoon in a bowl for more than half an hour reducing it to a somewhat liquid consistency, but not too much.

Finally pour in the raisins and put it in a smooth buttered mold dusted with powdered sugar mixed with flour, where the mixture does not reach half the pan which you will place well covered in a warm place or in a place of warm temperature to rise, which will take two or three hours.
When it is well risen to reach the mouth of the pan, put it in the oven at moderate heat, turn it out while warm, dust it with powdered sugar or if you like (this is optional) sprinkle it with rum.

title: Lingua di Vitella (Cured Veal Tongue)
description: Prepared with veal tongue or beef, saltpeter, and onion.

ingredients.name: 1 veal tongue from a calf or beef
ingredients.sourceText: 1 veal tongue from a calf or beef

steps: Take a veal tongue and rub it thoroughly with 20-30 grams of saltpeter depending on size until it has drawn in the salt.
After twenty-four hours, wash it several times with cold water.
While still damp, rub it generously with salt and leave it for eight days, turning it each morning in the brine produced by the salt dissolving in water.
To cook, place it in a pot with cold water, its natural brine, a bouquet garni, and half an onion studded with two cloves.
Boil for three or four hours.
Peel it while still boiling, let it cool, and serve it.
It will be an excellent and refined cold dish if you surround it with gelatin (recipe No. 3).
It can also be served hot, alone or accompanied by potatoes or spinach.

steps: Boil the whole veal tongue in salted water, which will take about two hours.
Make a fine battutino (minced mixture) of celery and carrot, bring it to boil with a good measure of oil for five minutes and set aside.

Make another battuto with two salted anchovies that have been washed and cleaned of their bones, 50 grams of capers squeezed of vinegar, a good pinch of parsley, a piece of bread crumb about the size of an egg barely dampened in vinegar, onion about the size of a hazelnut, less than half a clove of garlic.
When everything is well chopped, work it with a knife blade and a drop of oil to make it united and pasty, then mix it with the previous celery and carrot battuto.
To make it liquid, add more oil and the juice of half a lemon, season with pepper and salt if needed. This is the sauce.
While the tongue is still hot, peel it, discard the papilla with its small bones, and cut the rest of the tongue into thin slices.
Cover the slices with the described sauce and serve it cold.

title: Lingua in Umido (Braised Beef Tongue)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, ham, and onion.

ingredients.name: One beef tongue, without the papilla, weighing approximately one kilogram

steps: Take a beef tongue and boil it just enough to be able to peel it

Make a generous soffritto with 50 grams of ham (fatty and lean), half a medium onion, celery, carrot and parsley, and place on heat with 50 grams of butter together with the tongue seasoned with salt and pepper
Once browned, finish cooking it with broth poured little by little and tomato juice or conserve; then strain the sauce
Separately make a beurre manié with 20 grams of butter and one level spoonful of flour
When it has taken on a hazelnut color, pour the sauce into it and return the tongue to it for further cooking over low heat
Serve it cut into thick slices about one centimeter with a garnish of celery or other vegetables finished in the same sauce

title: Lingue di Gatto (Cat Tongues)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, egg white, and butter.
steps: Place the butter in a bowl just as it is and begin to stir it with a spoon
Then pour in the sugar, then the flour and lastly the egg white, always working the mixture to reduce it to a homogeneous paste

Place it in a syringe with a disc with a round or square hole about one centimeter in size, and push it into a pan lightly greased with butter in the form of pieces one finger long, keeping them spaced out because, as they melt, they spread
Bake them in a country oven at moderate heat. With this dose you will obtain about fifty

title: Lombo di Maiale Ripieno (Stuffed Pork Loin)
description: Prepared with pork, fat, and bone marrow.
steps: Brown the milk-fed veal in butter and mince both this and the prosciutto and mortadella with a knife and then pound them in a mortar to reduce them to a fine paste. Pour this paste onto the cutting board, add to it the marrow, the Parmesan and the egg yolk, season sparingly with salt, pepper and nutmeg, and with the blade of a knife reduce it to a uniform paste. Now remove the superficial fat from the loin, debone it and then cut it into seven or eight scaloppine, but in such a way that they all remain joined at the base so that they can be opened like the pages of a book and spread a spoonful of the said paste over each one; then join them together to form a roll that you will sprinkle with salt and pepper and tie tightly with string.

Cover it with the pork caul, binding it with thread so that it adheres well, and cook it at low heat in a pot with nothing else. Three hours of cooking should be sufficient and it will serve eight people. It is a good dish, both hot and cold, and not heavy; but if served hot you can send it to the table accompanied by vegetables reheated in its fat. To cut it into slices one must carve it not in the direction of the divisions, but the opposite, which will make it look fine.

Stud each piece lengthwise with two lard strips seasoned with salt and pepper
Make a proportionate battute with onion the size of a large walnut, a small garlic clove, a celery rib, a small piece of carrot, and a pinch of parsley, all finely chopped

title: Maccheroni alla francese (Macaroni French Style)
description: Prepared with macaroni, cheese, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Give the macaroni two-thirds cooking in not too salted water
Place the broth on the fire and when it boils throw in the grated Gruyère and butter to dissolve them well with a spoon
Once obtained, pour it immediately over the macaroni already drained of water, and I say immediately, because otherwise the Gruyère sinks to the bottom and becomes pasty
Keep the macaroni on the fire until completely cooked making sure some sauce remains
When you remove it, season it with the aforesaid parmesan and serve it with more parmesan on the side, for those who not having delicate taste love spiciness

title: Maccheroni alla napoletana II (Neapolitan Macaroni II)
description: Prepared with macaroni, onion, and tomatoes.
steps: In a pan or pot, brown two large slices of onion with 30 grams of butter and two tablespoons of oil
When the onion, which naturally breaks apart while boiling, is well browned, squeeze it with a spoon and throw it away
In that fat at boiling point pour 500 grams of tomatoes and a good pinch of coarsely chopped basil; season with salt and pepper
Prepare the tomatoes beforehand because they must be peeled, cut into pieces and cleaned of seeds as much as possible
Season the macaroni with the condensed sauce, with 50 grams of raw butter and parmesan and send them to the table
These will be especially appreciated by those who would swim in tomato sauce
Instead of long macaroni, penne can be used, indeed these will take the sauce better

title: Maiale Arrostito nel Latte (Pork Roasted in Milk)
description: Prepared with pork, milk, and salt.

ingredients.name: a piece of pork loin weighing approximately 500 grams
ingredients.sourceText: a piece of pork loin weighing approximately 500 grams

steps: Take a piece of pork loin weighing approximately 500 grams, salt it and place it in a pot with 2.5 deciliters of milk.
Cover it and let it boil slowly until the milk is consumed.
Then increase the heat to brown it, and once this is done, drain away the fat and remove the piece of meat.
Add a little fresh milk to the remaining coagulated milk residue.
Mix, bring to a boil and use it to spread on slices of lightly toasted bread to serve as an accompaniment to the pork when serving hot at table.
A total of three deciliters of milk will suffice. Cooked this way the pork will have a delicate flavor and will not be cloying.

When they have become wrinkled and have taken on a brown color remove them and use them for the intended purpose.

title: Mele in gelatina (Apples in Jelly)
description: Prepared with apples, kirsch, and lemon.

ingredients.name: Reinette apples or other fine quality, not too ripe, 650-700 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Reinette apples or other fine quality, not too ripe, 650-700 grams

steps: Remove the cores from the apples using a tin tube, peel them and immediately place them in fresh water where half a lemon has been squeezed
Dissolve the sugar in half a litre of water on the fire, united with a spoonful of kirsch, and pour it over the apples that you will have placed all together in a saucepan
Cook them so that they remain whole, then remove them dry and place them in a fruit dish
When cooled, fill and top the holes left by the cores with Currant Jelly (recipe 739), which being red stands out against the white of the apples and makes them beautiful

title: Migliaccio di Farina Dolce (Chestnut Flour Cake)

steps: Pass the chestnut flour through a sieve to make it soft since it clumps easily
Put it in a container and season with a scant pinch of salt
Mix it with 8 decilitres of cold water poured gradually to make a liquid batter

Cover the bottom with a light layer of oil
Spread two spoonfuls of oil over the batter when it is in the pan
Bake in an oven or between two fires
Turn it out hot

title: Migliaccio di Romagna (Pork Blood Cake from Romagna)
description: A cake made with pork, honey, and blanched almonds.
steps: Pound the almonds in a mortar together with the candied fruit, which you will have first cut into small pieces, moisten them from time to time with a few spoonfuls of milk and pass them through a sieve.

Place the milk on the fire with the lemon zest, which is then to be removed, and let it boil for ten minutes; add the grated chocolate to it, and when this is melted, remove it from the fire and let it cool a little.

Then pour the blood, already passed through a sieve, into the same pot along with all the other ingredients, reserving the breadcrumbs for last, of which, if there is too much, you can leave some behind.

Put the mixture to cook in a bain-marie and stir it often with a spoon so it does not stick to the pot. The cooking and the degree of density required are known from the spoon which, left in the middle of the mixture, must remain upright. If this does not happen, add the rest of the breadcrumbs, supposing you have not poured it all in.

Pour it into a pan lined with Pasta matta and, when it is completely cooled, cut it into almond shapes. Cook the pasta matta briefly so you can cut it easily and do not let the migliaccio dry out over the fire, but remove it when a pomegranate twig immersed in it comes out clean.

If you use honey instead of sapa, taste before adding the sugar so it does not turn out too sweet, and note that one of the merits of this dish is that it be well blended, that is, of fine composition.

title: Minestra del Paradiso (Paradise Soup)

ingredients.name: fine breadcrumbs from hard bread
ingredients.sourceText: 4 tablespoons fine breadcrumbs from hard bread

title: Minestra di Erbe Passate (Strained Herb Soup)
description: A soup made with beet, spinach, and lettuce.
steps: Remove the coarse ribs from the beet greens, cut all the greens roughly and soak them in fresh water for several hours.

Make a mixture with a quarter onion and all the herbs (parsley, celery, carrot and some basil or dill leaves); put it in a pan with a piece of butter and when well colored, add the herbs (drained somewhat), together with some tomatoes cut into pieces and a potato sliced.
Season with salt and pepper and let boil, stirring often.
When the greens are wilted, add hot water and cook until completely disintegrated.
Pass through a strainer, keeping the strained liquid for cooking rice or for wetting soup.
Before serving, taste it and add seasoning, especially butter, which will almost always be necessary.
Serve with Parmesan cheese on the side, but avoid making it too thick so it does not resemble plaster.

description: A soup made with breadcrumbs, beef marrow, and parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: nutmeg or lemon zest, or both together
ingredients.sourceText: nutmeg or lemon zest, or both together

Boil them in broth and serve

title: Minestra di Semolino Composta I (Composed Semolina Soup I)
description: A soup made with semolina, cheese, and milk.
steps: Cook fine grain semolina in milk and throw in enough so it turns out quite firm.
When you remove it from the fire season it with salt, grated parmigiano, a small piece of butter and a hint of nutmeg and let it cool.
Then dissolve the mixture with eggs until you reduce it like a liquid cream.
Take a smooth tin mold, grease the bottom well with butter, stick to it an equally greased sheet and pour the said mixture into it to set it in a bain-marie with fire on top.
Once cooked and cooled, a knife blade passed all around and the paper at the bottom will help you unmold it.
Cut it into small bricks or pieces the thickness of a coin and one or two centimeters wide and throw them into broth making them boil for a few minutes.
One glass of milk and two eggs is enough to make soup for four or five people.

title: Nasello alla Palermitana (Hake Palermo Style)
description: Prepared with hake, breadcrumbs, and anchovies.
steps: Take a hake weighing 500 to 600 grams, remove all the fins except the tail fin, leaving the head on.
Split it along the belly to remove the innards and the spine, flatten it, and season with a little salt and pepper.
Turn it to the back side, oil it, season with salt and pepper, bread it, then place it supine with two tablespoons of oil on a heat-proof dish or baking sheet.

Take three large salted anchovies (or four if small), clean them of scales and spines, mince them, and put them on the fire with two tablespoons of oil to break them down, being careful they do not boil.
Spread this sauce on the fish on the upper part, that is on the belly, and cover it completely with breadcrumbs, sprinkling some rosemary leaves on top if desired.
Cook it between two fires and let it form a crust, but be careful it does not dry out too much; for this reason, sprinkle more oil on it, and before removing it, squeeze a large lemon half over it.
It should be enough for four or five people if served at table surrounded by croutons with caviar or anchovies.

title: Pallottole di Mandorle (Almond Balls)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, powdered sugar, and chocolate.

ingredients.name: Grated or powdered chocolate, about 40 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Grated or powdered chocolate, about 40 grams

steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the sun or by the fire and pound them very finely with two tablespoons of the said sugar.
Pour them from the mortar into a vessel, add the remaining sugar and knead the mixture with the said liqueur.

Spread the chocolate on a work surface and form from the aforementioned mixture as many balls slightly larger than hazelnuts, of which you will obtain more than 30; roll them on the chocolate so they remain well covered, and you will be able to keep them for a long time.

title: Pan di Fegato (Liver Pâté)
description: Prepared with veal liver, bread, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Slice the liver into thin slices and cut the chicken livers in two parts, and throw these two things in a pan with the bay leaf and half the butter and when they have absorbed it add the other half and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the Marsala and after 4 or 5 minutes at most on high heat, the liver must remain tender; remove it dry and together with the bay leaf pound it in a mortar.

In the sauce that remains in the pan, crumble the bread crumb and make a paste which you will also throw in the mortar, then pass everything through a sieve; then add the Parmesan and the eggs, diluting the mixture with the said gravy or broth.
Finally place it in a smooth mold with paper underneath, greased with butter, and set it in a bain-marie.
Unmold it warm and when it is cold cover it all with gelatin from recipe 3, inside a mold of greater circumference than the first.
It will be enough for twelve people.

title: Pane di Sabbia (Sand Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with powdered sugar, rice flour, and starch flour.

ingredients.name: Juice of one quarter of a lemon
ingredients.sourceText: Juice of one quarter of a lemon

steps: Work the butter alone first, then add the egg yolks one by one, always stirring the spoon in the same direction
Then pour in the sugar, then the cognac and lemon juice
Then the flours and lastly the baking soda and whipped egg whites; but of these latter, pour in first two tablespoons to soften the mixture, and fold in the rest gently

Pour the mixture into a proportioned pan, greased with butter and dusted with powdered sugar and flour, and bake it in the oven or in a country oven at moderate heat. About one hour of baking should be sufficient

title: Pappardelle all'Aretina (Wide Ribbon Pasta Aretine-Style)
description: Prepared with duck, ham, and onion.
steps: Put the duck in a casserole with a piece of butter, season it with salt and pepper and, when it has taken color, add a finely chopped battuto of ham, onion, celery and carrot.

Let it wilt under the duck, turning it often; then remove a good part of the fat as an indigestible thing, and finish cooking it with broth and water poured little by little, in such a quantity that you have sauce left to season the pappardelle.

Get a piece of veal or beef spleen, open it and scrape out the inner part with a knife to boil it under the duck when this is cooked and it will serve as an ingredient for the sauce to which it is good to add also tomato and nutmeg.
Make a sheet of egg pasta, thick like that of tagliatelle and with the fluted wheel cut strips wider than a finger.
Cook them briefly and season them with the said sauce, with the duck liver in pieces, parmesan and a little butter if needed.
These pappardelle serve as a first course and the duck as a second course.

title: Pasta Sfoglia (Puff Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with flour, butter, and water.

ingredients.name: Fine flour or Hungarian flour, 200 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Fine flour or Hungarian flour, 200 grams

ingredients.name: Butter the size of a walnut
ingredients.sourceText: Butter the size of a walnut

steps: In winter, mix the flour with hot water that is not boiling, salt to taste, one spoonful of aquavit and butter the size of a walnut, taken from the aforementioned 150 or 200 grams. Once you have formed a dough that is neither too firm nor too soft, work it extensively, at least half an hour, first with your hands, then by throwing it forcefully against the work surface. Shape it into a rectangular loaf, wrap it in a kitchen cloth and let it rest briefly.

In the meantime, work the butter, if it is firm, with a hand dampened in water on the work surface to make it smooth and uniformly tender throughout. Then shape it into a loaf like that of the flour and place it in a bowl of fresh water. When the dough has rested, remove the butter from the water, dry it with a cloth and dust it thoroughly with flour.

Roll out the dough with a rolling pin only as much as necessary to enclose the butter loaf. Place the butter in the center and fold the edges of the dough over it, joining them together with your fingers and ensuring it adheres to the butter in all parts so no air remains between them.

Now begin to roll it out first with your hands, then with the rolling pin, thinning it out the first time as much as you can, being careful that the butter does not burst through. If this happens, immediately sprinkle a bit of flour where the butter appears, and frequently dust flour on the work surface and rolling pin so that the dough slides and stretches beneath it.

After the first rolling, fold the dough in three, like three overlapping sheets, and roll it out again to a reasonable thickness. Repeat this operation six times in total, letting the dough rest for ten minutes from time to time. On the last, which would be the seventh, fold it in two and reduce it to the thickness needed, that is something less than one centimeter.
Except for this last folding, make sure to give the dough a rectangular shape each time you stretch it, three times longer than it is wide, and if air pockets appear, prick them with a needle.

A marble slab would be better than a common work surface as it is colder and smoother. In summer, ice is necessary, both to firm up the butter before using it and to stretch the dough better, which is achieved by passing ice over the dough when necessary, wrapped in a very tight kitchen cloth or, better, placed between two plates covered with ice.

With puff pastry, as you know, one makes vol-au-vent, small pastries with jam or preserves, and pies filled with marzipan. If you wish to use the pastries as an intermediate course, fill them with a delicate mixture of meat, liver and sweetbreads. But in all ways these pastries should be glazed with egg yolk on the surface but not on the edges to avoid preventing puffing. If they are for dessert, dust them while hot with powdered sugar.

title: Paste alla Cacciatora (Pasta Hunter-Style)
description: Prepared with pasta, ducks, and celery.

ingredients.name: pasta (small shapes like nocette, paternostri, penne)
ingredients.sourceText: pasta (small shapes like nocette, paternostri, penne)

steps: Discard the head, feet, tail and intestines of the teal to boil them with a bunch garnished with celery, carrot and parsley stems in enough salted water to cook the pasta.
When cooked, bone them and chop them with a crescent-shaped knife together with the livers and gizzards emptied that you will have cooked with the teal.
Cook the pasta in the said broth, drain it well and season it in layers with this chopped meat, butter and parmesan in good measure.
This makes a tasty pasta and, what matters more, of not difficult digestion.

title: Paste con le Arzavole (Pasta with Teal)
description: Prepared with pasta, duck, and onion.
steps: Clean and prepare the teal, place it in a pot with a battuto of onion, a piece of celery, half a carrot, 40 grams of ham and a piece of butter; season with salt and pepper.
When browned, finish cooking it with good broth and a little tomato sauce or preserve.
Then bone it and chop it together with some pieces of dried mushrooms if you had them united to the teal while it was cooking.

Return to the fire this mixture with the aroma of spices or nutmeg and a piece of butter kneaded with flour to bind it, and with it and parmesan season 350 grams of pasta which can be macaroni, strips, penne or other similar shapes.
This quantity can be enough for five people if they are not big eaters.
If you add 50 grams of beef fillet to the teal you will have a more substantial sauce.

Return to the fire this mixture with the aroma of spices or nutmeg and a piece of butter kneaded with flour to bind it, and with it and parmesan season 350 grams of pasta which can be macaroni, strips, penne or other similar shapes.
This quantity can be enough for five people if they are not big eaters.
If you add 50 grams of beef fillet to the teal you will have a more substantial sauce.

title: Pastella per Fritti di Carne (Batter for Fried Meat)
description: Prepared with flour, oil, and eggs.
steps: Mix three heaping teaspoons of flour with two teaspoons of oil, add two eggs, a pinch of salt and mix well. This mixture will take on the appearance of a flowing cream and will serve to coat fried brain, sweetbreads, pancreas, lamb testicles, head of milk-fed veal and similar items. These things, some more some less, according to their nature, blanch them all, including the brain and sweetbreads which firm up when boiled. Salt the water and add a pinch of salt and pepper when you remove them from the water. Cut the pancreas into fillets lengthwise. Keep the sweetbreads about half a finger long. If the sweetbreads are from lamb, leave them whole. Cut the brains into pieces the size of a walnut, and keep the heads at a somewhat larger size. Toss the pieces in the batter after flouring them and fry them in pure lard or oil. These white fried items are often served with liver or milk-fed veal cutlets. Slice the liver very thinly, beat the cutlets with the back of a knife or mince the meat with a chopper to reunite it afterward into an elegant shape. Season both with salt and pepper, place them in a bath of beaten egg, and after a few hours, before frying them, roll them in fine breadcrumbs, repeating the operation even twice if necessary. Always accompany these fried items with lemon wedges.

title: Pasticcini di Pasta Beignet (Beignet Paste Small Cakes)
description: A cake made with water, flour, and butter.
steps: When the water boils pour all the flour at once and, stirring immediately, add the butter and keep it on the fire for 10 minutes, continuing always to stir it.
It should turn out a hard paste which you will spread to the thickness of a finger and pound in a mortar together with one egg to soften it somewhat.
Having obtained this, put it in a bowl to work it with a wooden spoon, adding the other eggs one at a time, whipping the whites.
Do not tire of working it until it is reduced like an ointment; let it rest for a few hours, and then put it in spoonfuls (which will be about ten or twelve) in a buttered baking pan.
Whisk one egg yolk with a little white to make it more fluid, brush them and smooth them with a small brush (but this supplement is not necessary), then put them in a well-heated oven.

When they are cooked make a slit on one side with a small knife, or in the shape of a half-circle on the underside, to fill them with cream or fruit preserves, sprinkle them with powdered sugar and serve them.
I warn you that when you work pastes that must puff up, the wooden spoon instead of moving it in circles is better to move it from bottom to top.

title: Pasticcini di Pasta Beignet Coperti di Cioccolata (Beignet Pastries Covered with Chocolate)
description: A pastry dish made with chocolate, cream or whipped cream or fruit or preserves or filling, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: Cream, whipped cream, or fruit preserves for filling
ingredients.sourceText: Cream, whipped cream, or fruit preserves for filling

steps: Prepare 20 to 23 small beignets following recipe N. 631.
Fill them with cream, whipped cream, or fruit preserves.
Whip the following mixture in the chocolate pot on the fire: chocolate, powdered sugar and water.
When well whipped, like chocolate served in a cup, pour it while boiling over the pastries placed one by one on a serving platter where they form a mound.
This is a dish best made the same day it is to be served, otherwise it hardens.
This quantity will suffice for six people.

title: Pasticcio di Carciofi e Piselli (Artichoke and Pea Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with artichokes, peas, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Clean the artichokes of all hard inedible leaves, divide them in half and remove the fuzzy center if present.
Give the artichokes and peas a brief half-cooking of a few minutes in salted water, then transfer them to fresh water, lift them out, and dry them well; divide the artichokes in half again.
Place both the artichokes and peas on the fire with 40 grams of the mentioned butter, season with salt and pepper, and finish cooking them with meat broth.
With the remaining 10 grams of butter, 1 tablespoon of flour and the aforesaid broth, make a kind of béchamel to bind the mixture.
Place the mixture in a fireproof dish and season it in layers with this béchamel and Parmesan cheese.
Cover it with the shortcrust pastry noted below; brush it with egg yolk, bake the pie in a country oven and serve it hot because it loses much if left to cool.
This quantity can serve seven or eight people.

title: Pasticcio di lepre (Hare Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with hare, veal, and tongue.

ingredients.name: Half hare without head and paws, one kilogram
ingredients.sourceText: Half hare without head and paws, one kilogram

ingredients.name: Fat and lean ham, cut thick half a finger, 50 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Fat and lean ham, cut thick half a finger, 50 grams

steps: After washing and drying the hare, remove 80 grams of lean meat from the fillet and set aside, then separate all meat from bones, break the bones and set aside, cut the meat into pieces and with the 80 grams of lean meat left whole, put it in infusion with about two-thirds of the marsala and with the following aromatics cut roughly: a quarter of a large onion, half a carrot, one celery rib about a palm long, several parsley stems and two bay leaves, season with salt and pepper, turn everything well and let it rest for several hours
Meanwhile clean the veal of membranes, chop it with a knife and pound it in a mortar as fine as possible

Drain the hare meat from the marsala and with all the bones, the indicated aromatics, the ham fat cut into small pieces and 30 grams of the butter, put it in a covered pot and at high heat let it brown well, stirring often with a spoon and basting, when dry, with marsala, also using the remaining infusion, and with broth until completely cooked
Then separate the meat from the bones again and set aside the 80 grams of lean for forming with this, with 50 grams of ham and with the tongue, so many fillets thicker than half a finger

First pound all the hare meat in a mortar, basting it from time to time to make it more pasty but not too liquid, with the rest of the marsala and with broth and pass it; then pound the bones and ensure that as much as possible of these passes through, using a wire sieve for this purpose

Make a béchamel with 30 grams of the butter, the indicated flour and milk and, when cooked, pour into the same pot all the passed meat, both that of the hare and the raw veal, add the two eggs, mix well and taste the mixture to see if it is seasoned correctly, adding salt and the rest of the butter if needed

Now line the pie with the pasta described below and to fill it follow recipe 370, cut the truffles into chunks the size of hazelnuts and thus raw and with all the fillets described arrange them in three layers alternated with the well pressed mixture so they are spread regularly and make a fine show when the pie is cut, finally spread the 30 grams of ham in rather thin slices on top and cover it

You can cover it with puff pastry at half, like that of recipe 155, or with the following: flour 250 grams, butter 80 grams, wine spirit 2 teaspoons, sugar 2 teaspoons, egg yolks 2 numbers, the juice of one lemon wedge, salt 5 grams, cold water if needed
With this method, except for some variations as needed, you can make several other game pies, such as wild boar, fallow deer and roe deer, this should be enough for a meal even for twenty people

title: Pasticcio di Magro (Lean Pastry Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with fish, rice, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: white wine or Marsala two spoonfuls
ingredients.sourceText: white wine or Marsala two spoonfuls

steps: Cook the rice with 40 grams of butter and a quarter of chopped onion, salt it, and when cooked with the necessary water bind it with the said eggs and 30 grams of Parmesan. Make a soffritto with onion, butter, celery, carrot and parsley and in it cook the mushrooms cut into slices, the peas, and the artichokes cut into wedges and half-cooked. Finish cooking these things with a few spoonfuls of hot water and season them with salt, pepper and 50 grams of grated Parmesan when you have removed them from the fire. Cook the fish, which can be mullet, a type of fish, or even cut fish, in a soffritto of oil, garlic, parsley, tomato juice or tomato paste and season it with salt and pepper. Remove the fish, pass its sauce and in this dissolve the pine nuts that you have first toasted and crushed. Remove from the fish the head, backbone and small bones, cut it into pieces, return it to its sauce and add everything except the rice. Now that the elements of the pie are all ready, make the pastry to enclose it with the following amounts: flour 400 grams, butter 80 grams, eggs 2, white wine or Marsala two spoonfuls, a pinch of salt. Take any mold, grease it with butter and line it with the said pastry rolled thin; then fill it by first pouring in half the rice, then all the filling and on top of the filling the rest of the rice, covering it at the mouth with the same pastry. Cook it in the oven, unmold it and serve it lukewarm or cold. Made in the indicated amounts it will be enough for twelve people.
