title: Pasticcio Freddo di Cacciagione (Cold Game Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with partridge, chicken, and egg yolk.

ingredients.name: One partridge (gray partridge or red partridge), somewhat aged
ingredients.sourceText: One partridge (gray partridge or red partridge), somewhat aged

ingredients.name: Marsala, two fingers of a common glass
ingredients.sourceText: Marsala, two fingers of a common glass

ingredients.name: Small battuto of onion, carrot, and celery
ingredients.sourceText: Small battuto of onion, carrot, and celery

steps: Clean the partridge, wash it, and put it on the fire with the battuto, butter, prosciutto cut into slices, whole bay leaves, and season with salt and pepper.
When the onion takes on color, wet it with marsala poured little by little, and if it is not enough to bring the partridge to half-cooked, use broth.
Remove the partridge from the fire, take the breast and make eight fillets that you will set aside.
Cut the rest into small pieces to cook completely, together with the chicken livers, including that of the partridge.
When cooked, remove it dry and put it in a mortar, discarding the bay leaves.

Into the remaining sauce, throw the bread marrow and with a little broth, stirring, make a paste that you will pour also into the mortar, as well as the scrapings of the truffles, and pound everything well and fine to pass through a sieve.
In this paste, blend the egg yolk and work it well with a spoon to make it creamy.
Make the pastry to cover it using recipe No. 372.
Take one of those special molds for these pies, which are made in the shape of a boat or round, fluted, of white iron, with a hinge that opens.

Grease it with butter and, having rolled out the pastry thin slightly more than a coin, line it with the same and make the bottom which you will place on a copper baking sheet also greased with butter.

First throw into the bottom part of the mixture and arrange on top part of the fillets (breast of the partridge and tongue) and some pieces of truffles as big as hazelnuts and raw; then other mixture interspersed with truffles and fillets and so on if the pie were voluminous.
Press it well so that it comes together unified and compact and make it a cover of the same pastry with some ornament, leaving in the middle a hole so that the vapor escapes.
Gild it on the outside and bake it in the oven or in a country oven, and when you take it out cover the hole with a knot of the same pastry, made to measure and baked separately.

title: Pastine pel Thè (Tea Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with potato flour, powdered sugar, and egg whites.
steps: Form a mound on the work surface with the two flours and sugar mixed together

Make a hole in the middle, place the egg whites and butter in pieces, and with the blade of a knife first and with your hands after, using the milk, knead it and work it for about half an hour to obtain a rather soft paste

Roll it out with a rolling pin into a sheet the thickness of a coin, cut it into round disks like those of N. 7, perforate them with the tines of a fork and bake them in the oven or in a country oven in a butter-greased pan
With only half the dose of the recipe, you will obtain quite a lot

title: Pere in Composta II (Pears in Compote II)
description: Prepared with pears, lemon, and sugar.
steps: Squeeze the lemon into the water and set it aside

Place the pears on the fire covered with water and boil them for four or five minutes; then throw them into fresh water, peel them, cut half of their stem off, and as you peel them drop them into the water prepared with lemon
Having done this, take the same water, pass it through a strainer, put it on the fire and when it begins to boil pour in the sugar and let it boil somewhat
Then throw in the pears to cook them, but in such a way that they do not fall apart
Remove them dry, place them in a compote dish, reduce the syrup and pour it over the pears, passing it through the strainer once more
If they are very large pears, cut them into wedges after they have undergone the first boiling
Serve them cold

title: Piccione a Sorpresa (Surprise Pigeon)
description: Prepared with pigeon, veal or cutlet or milk, and chicken.

ingredients.name: One veal cutlet or milk veal cutlet
ingredients.sourceText: One veal cutlet or milk veal cutlet

steps: If you have a pigeon to put on the spit and want it to serve more than one person, fill it with a veal cutlet or milk veal cutlet of proportionate size.

Beat the cutlet well to make it thinner and more tender, season it with salt, pepper, a pinch of spices and some pieces of butter, roll it up and place it inside the pigeon, sewing the opening closed.
If you add slices of truffles to the seasoning mentioned above, it will be even better.

You can also cook separately the small onion and the pigeon's liver in sauce or butter, mash them and use them to spread on the cutlet; in this way the different aroma of the two types of meat blends together and forms a better flavor.
What has been said for the pigeon applies equally to a chicken.

title: Piccione all'inglese (English-style Squab)
description: Prepared with squab, veal or chicken breast, and ham.

ingredients.name: Lean veal, 100 grams, or one chicken breast
ingredients.sourceText: Lean veal, 100 grams, or one chicken breast

ingredients.name: Thin slices of fatty and lean ham, 40 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Thin slices of fatty and lean ham, 40 grams

ingredients.name: Half a glass of good defatted broth
ingredients.sourceText: Half a glass of good defatted broth

steps: Cut the squab into small pieces at its joints, discarding the head and feet.
Cut the veal or chicken breast into small rolled pieces and beat them with the back of a knife.
Cut the ham and tongue into strips one finger wide.
Cut the egg into eight wedges.

Take an oval metal or porcelain plate that can withstand fire and arrange in layers one on top of the other: first half of the squab and veal, then half of the ham and tongue, half of the butter scattered here and there in small pieces, and half, that is four wedges, of the egg; season with very little salt, pepper, and a hint of spices, and repeat the operation with the remainder so that the whole makes a mound.
Finally pour the aforementioned broth, but cold, which you will see floating on the first edge of the plate and which will remain largely after cooking.
For the pastry: mix the flour with the aforementioned ingredients (spirit of wine, sugar, lemon juice, egg yolk, and salt), and if they are not enough, add tepid water to make a rather soft dough.

Work it very much by throwing it with force against the pastry board, let it rest a little, and roll it out by folding it four or five times, reducing it finally to the thickness of a shield with the striped rolling pin.
Cover the plate with it, adorning it, if possible, with trimmings of the same pastry, then gild it with egg yolk.
Cook this pastry (which can be called such) in a country oven and serve it hot.

Alternatively, give the squab and other meats a partial cooking first with the butter, seasoning them with salt, pepper, and spices, then arrange them on the platter in the indicated manner, not excluding the cooking juices and broth. You can increase the seasoning and also add chicken giblets, sweetbreads, and truffles.

title: Piccione in Gratella (Pigeon on the Grill)
description: Prepared with pigeon, breadcrumbs, and oil.
steps: Take a large but young pigeon, divide it in two lengthwise and flatten the pieces well with your hands.
Then place them to fry in oil for four or five minutes, just enough to firm up the meat.
Season it while hot with salt and pepper, then prepare it in this manner: melt {{source-4}} over heat without letting it boil; beat an egg and mix one with the other.
Dip the pigeon well in this mixture and after some time roll it entirely in breadcrumbs.
Cook it on the grill over slow heat and serve it with a sauce or side dish.

title: Piselli alla Francese I (Peas French Style I)
description: Prepared with peas, onions, and broth.

ingredients.name: Butter, 30 grams at first, then another 30 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Butter, 30 grams at first, then another 30 grams

steps: Take two young onions, cut them in half lengthwise, enclose some parsley stems in the middle and tie them.
Put them on the fire with 30 grams of butter and when browned, pour over them a good ladleful of broth.
Let boil and when the onions are very soft, strain them, squeezing them together with the juice, which you will return to the fire with the peas and two whole heads of lettuce.
Season with salt and pepper and let them boil slowly.
At the halfway point of cooking add another 30 grams of butter mixed with one tablespoon not heaping of flour and pour broth if needed.
Before serving, bind them with two egg yolks dissolved in a little broth. In this way they turn out very delicate.

title: Piselli alla Francese II (Peas French Style II)
description: Prepared with peas, onion, and broth.
steps: Slice a good amount of onion into very thin slices and put it on the fire in a pot with a piece of butter.
When well browned, pour in a pinch of flour, stir, and then add, depending on the quantity, one or two ladlefuls of broth and let the flour cook.
Pour in the peas, season with salt and pepper, and at the halfway point of cooking add one or two whole heads of lettuce.
Boil slowly, taking care that the liquid does not become too thick.
Some sweeten the peas with a teaspoon of sugar; but in this case use little, because the sweetness should seem natural and not added artificially.
When you serve them remove the lettuce.

title: Pizza a Libretti (Folded Fried Pizza)
description: Prepared with cognac, oil or lard, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: cognac or spirits, three tablespoons (or fumetto)
ingredients.sourceText: cognac or spirits, three tablespoons (or fumetto)

steps: Roll out a sheet of dough not too firm and as thin as possible by mixing flour with two eggs, a pinch of salt and three tablespoons of cognac or spirits, or perhaps better fumetto.

Once the sheet is made, grease it with 20 grams of melted butter and roll it, or fold it over itself to the width of 10 to 11 centimeters, but so that the greased part remains inside; then cut the roll in half lengthwise and then crosswise at proportionate distances to obtain many rectangles and press with your fingers the outer edge of these, that is the rib that has not been cut.
Fry them in a pan with plenty of fat and before serving dust them with powdered sugar.
If they turn out well you will see that these little books open and remain flaked.
This dose can be enough for four people.

title: Plum-pudding (English Plum Pudding)
description: A pudding made with powdered sugar, raisins, and sultana.

ingredients.name: For every egg used to bind it, the following ingredients in these quantities:
ingredients.sourceText: For every egg used to bind it, the following ingredients in these quantities:

steps: Remove seeds from the zibibbo raisins; cut the candied fruits into short, thin strips; if you cannot obtain the suet from a castrated ram, take it from veal, and cut both this and the bread crumb into very small dice, removing the membranes from the suet
Make a mixture of everything, having previously beaten the eggs separately, and let it rest for some hours; then place it in a cloth and tie it very tightly with string to form a ball
Place a pot of water on the heat and when it boils immerse the pudding in it in such a way that it does not touch the bottom of the pot, letting it boil slowly for as many hours as there are eggs

Remove it from the cloth carefully, make a small well on top and, pouring in it a small glass or two of cognac or rum that spreads throughout the pudding, set it alight and thus hot and in flames send it to the table to be cut into slices and eaten when the flame is extinguished
Three eggs will be enough for six people

title: Pollastra in Umido col Contorno di Riso (Stewed Hen with Rice Border)
description: Prepared with hen, rice, and fat.

ingredients.name: One hen, empty, weighing approximately 700 grams
ingredients.sourceText: One hen, empty, weighing approximately 700 grams

ingredients.name: One onion, more than medium size
ingredients.sourceText: One onion, more than medium size

steps: Tie the hen to hold its parts together.
Put 30 grams of the butter and the ham cut into strips in a pot.
Chop the onion and carrot over it.
Place the hen breast-side down in the pot, seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Keep it covered and when browned on both sides, moisten it gradually with hot water until fully cooked, leaving enough sauce to flavor the rice, but strain the sauce.
Put the rice on the fire as is with half of the remaining butter.
Draw it to completion with hot water and finally with the hen's sauce.
When fully cooked, add the rest of the butter and give it greater flavor with a good handful of grated Parmesan.
Cook the liver and gizzard together with the hen and cut into pieces, mix them into the rice.
The risotto thus prepared can also serve as a soup and be enough for three people, but then serve the hen separately with some of its sauce and the mushrooms as a side dish.

title: Pollo al Diavolo (Deviled Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, butter or oil, and salt.

ingredients.name: One young rooster or young chicken
ingredients.sourceText: One young rooster or young chicken

steps: Take a young rooster or young chicken, remove the neck and legs, and open it completely along the front, flattening it as much as possible.
Wash and dry it well with a cloth, then place it on a grill.
When it begins to brown, turn it, brush it with melted butter or oil using a brush, and season it with salt and pepper.
When the opposite side begins to take color, turn it and treat it in the same manner.
Continue brushing it with butter or oil and seasoning it sufficiently, keeping it over the fire until it is cooked.

title: Pollo alla Cacciatora (Hunter-Style Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, onion, and oil or lard.

ingredients.name: half a glass of Sangiovese or other good red wine
ingredients.sourceText: half a glass of Sangiovese or other good red wine

steps: Slice a large onion and soak it in fresh water for more than half an hour, then dry it and put it in a pan with oil or lard.
When cooked, set it aside.
Cut up a chicken and fry it in the remaining fat, and when browned, add the said onion.
Season with salt and pepper and pour in half a glass of Sangiovese or other good red wine and some tomato juice.
After five minutes of boiling, serve it.
Note that this is not a dish for weak stomachs.

description: Prepared with hen, garlic, and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: One garlic clove, divided into four or five pieces
ingredients.sourceText: One garlic clove, divided into four or five pieces

steps: Lard the chicken with some sprigs of rosemary and with the garlic clove divided into four or five pieces.
Put it on the fire with minced lardoon and season it with salt and pepper inside and outside.
When it is browned on all sides, add tomatoes in pieces, having removed the seeds.
When these are broken down, moisten it with broth or water.
Separately in oil, lard or butter, brown some raw potatoes cut into wedges.
Let them take flavor in the chicken's sauce and serve them as a side dish.
Substitute butter for the lardoon if you want the chicken with a more delicate taste.

title: Pollo alla Marengo (Chicken Marengo)
description: Prepared with chicken, white wine, and broth.

ingredients.name: one young chicken, excluding the neck and legs
ingredients.sourceText: one young chicken, excluding the neck and legs

steps: Take a young chicken and, excluding the neck and legs, cut it into large pieces at the joints.
Sauté it with {{source-1}}, one spoonful of oil and season it with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Once the pieces are browned on both sides, drain off the fat and throw into the sauté pan one level spoonful of flour and one decilitre of white wine.

title: Pollo alla Rudinì (Chicken Rudinì)
description: Prepared with chicken, lemon, and egg.
steps: Take a young chicken, remove the neck, the wing tips, and cut the legs two fingers from the knee; then cut it into six pieces: two with the wings to each of which you will leave attached half of the breast, two with the thighs including the hip, and two with the back with the front part removed.
Remove the hip bones and the breast wishbone; crush the two back pieces.

Beat an egg with water equal to what fits in half an eggshell, place the chicken (after flouring it) in infusion in this mixture, and season it with pepper and salt in good measure, leaving it until the moment of cooking.
Then take the pieces one by one, coat them in breadcrumbs, and with a sauté pan or copper skillet over the fire with {{source-6}}, cook them in this manner.

When the butter begins to sizzle, place the chicken pieces skin side down for a moment, then turn them over, cover the pan with a lid and with much heat above and little below, leave them for about ten minutes.
Serve it with lemon wedges.

title: Pollo Disossato Ripieno (Boned and Stuffed Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, veal, and bread.

ingredients.name: Veal loin, approximately 300 grams (or proportionally less if the chicken is small)
ingredients.sourceText: Veal loin, approximately 300 grams (or proportionally less if the chicken is small)

ingredients.name: Bread crumb, one large piece soaked in broth
ingredients.sourceText: Bread crumb, one large piece soaked in broth

steps: Cut the neck in half, the wing tips, and the legs at the thigh joint.
Open the chicken along the back superficially, from the wings to the tail, and with a sharp knife begin to remove the bones of the wings from the inside, scraping the meat well.
Remove the bones of the hips and thighs from the inside.
Scraping with the knife the external bones of the carcass, remove it all in one piece, including the innards.
Leave the small bones of the breastbone, or remove it all and take out the breast fork.
Turn the thighs and wings, now stripped of bones, drawing them inward and remove all the tendons you find between the meat.
Finely mince the veal, then pound it in a mortar to reduce it very fine.
Add to this meat a large piece of bread soaked in broth, a handful of grated Parmesan, three egg yolks, salt, pepper and, if you like, nutmeg flavor.
Add to the mixture 20 grams of fat and lean ham and 20 grams of salted tongue, cut into small dice.
Fill the chicken and sew it closed.
Wrap it tightly in cloth and tie it.
Put it to cook in water for a couple of hours over low heat.
Remove the wrapping and let it brown first with butter, then in a sauce made as follows:
Break all the bones removed from the chicken, the neck and head included, and with dried meat in pieces, butter, onion, celery and carrot put them on the fire in a pot.
Season with salt and pepper, draw the sauce with the water in which the chicken has boiled, which has already become a good broth.
Before serving, alone or with a side dish, remove the thread with which it was sewn.

steps: Boil the chicken breast in water for half an hour until cooked through.
Remove the skin from the cooked chicken, debone it completely, and cut it into pieces.
Season the chicken pieces with salt (sparingly), pepper, and two tablespoons of oil.
Let the chicken sit on a platter for several hours.
Clean the anchovies of scales and bones. Finely chop the parsley with a mincing knife.
Pound the anchovies, parsley, tuna, and capers together in a mortar until the mixture is very fine.
Transfer the sauce to a bowl and dilute it with {{source-5}} and half a tablespoon of vinegar.
Coat half of the sauce over the chicken pieces and cover with the remaining half.
Garnish with hard-boiled eggs cut into wedges around the chicken when serving.

steps: Start by giving the sausages and giblets half-cooking in butter, moistening them with a little broth if needed; season with a little salt and a little pepper because of the sausages.
Remove them dry and in the remaining liquid throw a bread crumb to obtain, with a little broth, two spoonfuls of thick paste.

title: Polpettone di Carne Cruda alla Fiorentina (Raw Meat Meatloaf Florentine Style)
description: Prepared with veal, fat, and onion.

ingredients.name: half a kilogram of lean veal without bone
ingredients.sourceText: half a kilogram of lean veal without bone

ingredients.name: one slice of fat and lean prosciutto
ingredients.sourceText: one slice of fat and lean prosciutto

ingredients.name: onion (about the size of a walnut)
ingredients.sourceText: onion (about the size of a walnut)

ingredients.name: half a generous glass of water
ingredients.sourceText: half a generous glass of water

steps: Take half a kilogram of lean veal without bone, clean it of membranes and calluses, and mince it finely first with a knife, then with a crescent-shaped knife, together with a slice of fat and lean prosciutto.
Season with a little salt, pepper, and spices, add one egg, mix well, and with wet hands form it into a ball and dust with flour.

Make a small battuto with a little onion (about the size of a walnut), parsley, celery, and carrot, put it on the fire with a small piece of butter, and when it has taken color, throw in the meatloaf.

Brown it on all sides, then pour into the pan half a generous glass of water in which you have dissolved half a teaspoon of flour; cover it and let it boil over the lowest heat, watching that it does not stick.
When serving, squeeze half a lemon over it with its dense sauce around it.
If you want it Piedmont style, simply place a peeled hard-boiled egg in the center of the ball when forming it, which serves to give beauty to the meatloaf when sliced.

description: Prepared with meat, parmesan cheese, and bread.

ingredients.name: two or three tablespoons of bread paste
ingredients.sourceText: two or three tablespoons of bread paste

ingredients.name: bread marrow cooked in milk, broth, or water with a little butter
ingredients.sourceText: bread marrow cooked in milk, broth, or water with a little butter

steps: Remove the fat from the leftover meat and mince the lean part with a crescent-shaped knife.

Season it proportionally with salt, pepper, parmesan cheese, one or two eggs, and two or three tablespoons of bread paste made from bread marrow cooked in milk, broth, or water enriched with a little butter.
Mix everything together, form it into an oval loaf, and dust it with flour.
Fry it in lard or oil until it becomes firm and forms a crust on the surface.

title: Pomodori Ripieni (Stuffed Tomatoes)
description: Prepared with tomatoes, onion, and celery.
steps: Take medium-sized ripe tomatoes and cut them in half equally, remove the seeds, season with salt and pepper and fill the holes formed with the following mixture, so that it overflows and rises heaped on the surface of the tomato.

Make a battutino with onion, parsley and celery, put it on the fire with a piece of butter and when it takes color, pour in a handful of softened and finely chopped dried mushrooms; add a spoonful of pap with milk, season with salt and pepper, and boil somewhat, moistening the mixture with milk if needed.
Remove from fire and when lukewarm add grated Parmesan and an egg or just the yolk if sufficient to make the mixture not too liquid.
Cook the prepared tomatoes in a pan over two fires with a little butter and oil together and serve them as a side dish to any roast or grilled steak.

For serving alongside boiled meat they are excellent prepared as follows: take a wide pan or a baking sheet, scatter small pieces of butter on it and on top place, skin-side up, tomatoes cut in half after removing the seeds. Season with salt, pepper and a little oil, scatter more small pieces of butter on top and cook them in an uncovered pan.

title: Ponce alla Romana (Roman Punch Ice Cream)
description: Prepared with oranges, lemons, and egg whites.
steps: Boil for five or six minutes 250 grams of the said sugar in 4 deciliters of the said water, with a little peel of lemon and orange inside
Remove from fire, squeeze the juice of the oranges and lemons into this syrup, strain it through a cloth and pour it into the ice cream maker to freeze

title: Presnitz (Triestine Filled Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with sultana, walnuts, and sweet almonds.

ingredients.name: mixed spices of cinnamon, cloves and mace
ingredients.sourceText: 5 grams mixed spices of cinnamon, cloves and mace

steps: After cleaning the sultana raisins, soak them in the Cyprus wine and rum mixed together; let them sit like this for several hours and remove them when they begin to swell.

Cut the pine nuts into three parts crosswise, cut the candied fruits into very small dice, chop the walnuts and almonds with a crescent blade to about the size of rice, and the focaccia, which can be a dough similar to brioches or Milanese panettone, grate or crumble it.
Leave the raisins whole and then mix everything together, including the rum and Cyprus wine.
This is the filling; now it must be enclosed in puff pastry for which you can use the recipe from N. 155 in the proportion of {{source-12}} and {{source-13}}.
Roll it out tight, long and of a thickness a little more than a coin.
Spread the filling on it and make it into a roll like a sausage by pulling the pastry on the edges to join it.
Give it a circumference of about 10 centimeters, flatten it somewhat or leave it round, place it in a buttered copper pan coiled around itself like a serpent; but not too tight.
Finally, with a brush, coat it with a liquid mixture of melted butter and one egg yolk.
Instead of one you can make two, if you like, with this same dose, half of which I believe would be enough for seven or eight people.

title: Pudding Cesarino
description: A pudding made with bread, raisins, and sultana.

ingredients.name: Sugar for the mold, approximately 100 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Sugar for the mold, approximately 100 grams

ingredients.name: Marsala and rum combined, three tablespoonfuls total
ingredients.sourceText: Marsala and rum combined, three tablespoonfuls total

steps: Cut the bread crumb into thin slices and throw it into the milk
While waiting for this to soak, clean the raisins and remove the seeds from the malaga variety and prepare the form for cooking, which should be the one for puddings, made of worked copper

Melt the aforementioned approximately 100 grams of sugar in a saucepan over heat and when it has taken on a hazelnut color, pour it into the mold to coat it completely; when it has cooled, grease the sugar coating with fresh butter
To the soaked crumb add the aforementioned 250 grams of sugar, the egg yolks and liqueurs, stirring everything well
Finally add the raisins and the beaten egg whites
Cook it in a water bath for three full hours, with heat underneath only in the last hour
Serve it hot and in flames and therefore water it abundantly with rum and set it alight with a spoonful of lit spirits
This will be enough for ten or twelve people

title: Quenelles (French Dumplings)
description: Prepared with veal, tomato sauce, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: eggs, one whole and one yolk
ingredients.sourceText: eggs, one whole and one yolk

steps: Clean the veal well of membranes and the fat of the skin that covers it, and after weighing them, mince them as much as possible with a knife and crescent-shaped knife, then pound them in a mortar until reduced to a very fine paste.
Make a béchamel with the flour, butter, and milk mentioned above, and when it has cooled, unite it with the pounded mixture, the eggs, and seasoning of only salt, and mix everything together well.
Spread a veil of flour on the work surface, pour the mixture over it, and lightly floured, roll it into a stick shape to obtain 18 or 20 pieces similar to sausages, about one finger long.
Put water on the fire in a wide pan, and when it boils throw in the quenelles; let them boil for 8 or 10 minutes and you will see them puff up.

With a slightly perforated spoon, remove them dry and serve them swimming in tomato sauce N. 125, to which you will add some fresh or dried mushrooms (which you will have cooked beforehand in the same sauce) and some olives in brine, from which you will remove the pit.

You can substitute the tomato sauce with meat gravy, or garnish with the quenelles an offal stew. They can also be made with the white meat of chickens or with fish flesh, and this quantity can be enough for five people.

If you use the tomato sauce, which is most suitable for this delicate-flavored dish, bind it with a mixture composed of 30 grams of butter and one tablespoon of flour, pouring it into it when it has taken on a hazelnut color on the fire.

description: A biscuit made with white sugar, sweet almonds, and bitter almonds.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them well in the sun or by the fire and pound them very finely in a mortar with two tablespoons of the sugar, poured in several times; then mix in the rest of the sugar.

Beat the egg whites in a bowl and pour in the almonds thus prepared and the grated orange peel. Mix again with a spoon and pour the mixture onto the work surface over a light layer of flour to take only the small amount of flour needed to lightly roll with a rolling pin into a soft sheet, half a finger thick.
Cut them with the form marked below and you will obtain 16 to 18 to cook in the following way:

Take a baking sheet, make a layer of bran as high as a shield and cover it all with wafers to place the ricciarelli on and bake them in the oven at moderate heat so they remain tender. In the absence of an oven, which would be most suitable, use a country oven.
After cooking, cut away the wafer that protrudes from the edges of these pastries, which turn out to be of fine quality.

description: Prepared with milk, veal, and ham.

ingredients.name: 1 boneless, all lean braciole of milk-fed veal, weighing about 400 grams
ingredients.sourceText: 1 boneless, all lean braciole of milk-fed veal, weighing about 400 grams

ingredients.name: thick slice of cooked ham, fat and lean
ingredients.sourceText: 50 grams of thick slice of cooked ham, fat and lean

steps: Dampen the braciole with water and beat it with a meat mallet to reduce it to about one centimeter thickness.

Mince with a crescent knife the 120 grams of lean meat together with the 20 grams of ham, then pound them in the mortar adding the Parmesan, butter, egg, little salt and little pepper to make from these ingredients the compound to keep together the filling you will form as follows.
Cut into strips more than one centimeter thick the chicken breast and the two slices of mortadella and ham.
Spread the compound on one part of the braciole and on top of it place one third of the fillets, intercalating them, then spread more on top and thus for two more times.
Roll up the braciole with the filling inside and tie it like a salami to put it on the fire with 30 grams of butter, salt and pepper in scant measure.
When it has taken color, drain off the fat, which can be used for some other dish, and continue cooking for about three hours with broth added little by little.

description: A pastry dish made with calf sweetbreads or milk or veal or chicken, sauce, and béchamel.

ingredients.name: Animelle (calf sweetbreads) or milk veal or chicken livers
ingredients.sourceText: Animelle (calf sweetbreads) or milk veal or chicken livers

ingredients.name: Salted tongue or prosciutto (fat and lean), finely diced
ingredients.sourceText: Salted tongue or prosciutto (fat and lean), finely diced

steps: If using animelle, place them in a pan with a small piece of butter, season with salt and pepper, and when they take on color, finish cooking them with sauce N. 4
Cut the cooked animelle to the size of a chickpea or smaller
To the animelle add 1 or 2 spoonfuls of béchamel sauce N. 137, some salted tongue or finely diced prosciutto (fat and lean), a pinch of parmigiano, and a pinch of nutmeg
Ensure the ingredients are in proportions that render the mixture of pleasant and delicate flavor

steps: Cook this meat together with a small mixture of shallot or onion, parsley, celery, carrot and butter. Season with salt, pepper and spices, moistening it with broth. Remove it dry from the heat, remove the tender parts from the gizzard, add several pieces of softened dried mushrooms, a slice of fatty and lean prosciutto and chop everything very finely with a chopper. Into the liquid remaining from cooking the meat, throw a piece of bread marrow to make one spoonful of thick paste. Mix it into the mixture, add a good pinch of Parmesan and two eggs, and fill the chicken with all of this and sew it shut. You can cook it boiled or braised. If you cook it boiled you will have excellent broth, but be careful to carve it to extract the filling all in one piece which you will then slice. Another filling for chickens is that of roasted chicken no. 539.

title: Risotto coi gamberi (Risotto with Shrimp)
description: Prepared with shrimp, rice, and onion.
steps: Make an abundant soffritto with half an onion, three cloves of garlic, carrot, celery and parsley and place it on the fire with oil in proportion
When the soffritto has taken color, throw in the shrimp and season with salt and pepper
Turn them often and when all have become red, moisten them with tomato sauce or paste and shortly after pour in enough hot water to suffice for the rice
Let boil not too long, since shrimp cooks quickly, then remove them dried and set aside a quarter of the largest ones after shelling them
Pound the remaining shrimp in a mortar, pass them through a sieve and mix the strained pulp into the broth where they were cooked

Place a piece of butter on the fire in a pot and pour in the cleaned rice without washing it; stir continuously and when the rice has taken the sheen of the butter, pour in the broth hot little by little
At more than half cooking add the whole shelled shrimp and before serving give it grace with a handful of parmesan cheese

ingredients.name: Peas from recipe No. 427, in proper proportion

Salt it and cook until dry, adding the remaining butter
Before removing from the fire, add the peas in proper proportion and give it flavor with a good handful of Parmesan cheese

title: Risotto coi ranocchi (Risotto with Frogs)
description: Prepared with rice, onion, and carrot.

ingredients.name: Frogs, twelve large ones for 300 grams of rice
ingredients.sourceText: Frogs, twelve large ones for 300 grams of rice

ingredients.name: One quarter of a large onion
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter of a large onion

steps: To make the frog meat tender, throw them in hot water just after skinning and then pass them in fresh water, but be careful—only half a minute, or you will cook them
Leave behind the thighs; do not use the eggs in this case
Make a battuto with one quarter of a large onion, one clove of garlic, carrot, celery, parsley, basil and put it on the fire with oil, pepper and salt
When it has taken color throw in the frogs, stir from time to time and once browned throw in pieces of tomatoes, which you will let fall apart
Then pour in as much hot water as may be needed
Boil slowly until the frogs are well cooked and then pass everything through a strainer, squeezing well
In a little of this broth cook the thighs set aside, bone them and unite them with the rest
Put the rice on the fire with a piece of butter, stir, and when the butter has been completely absorbed pour the hot frog broth one ladle at a time until completely cooked
Before removing the rice throw into it a handful of Parmesan cheese and serve it

ingredients.name: One whole egg and one egg yolk

Mix these with the sugar into the flour
Make a well in the mass to place the remaining ingredients and knead it working as little as possible

Cut with a disc or similar tool to obtain about 50 small pastries
Bake in a countryside oven after placing them on a baking pan greased lightly with cold butter

title: Salsa del Papa (Pope's Sauce)
description: A sauce made with capers, olives, and onion.

ingredients.name: Pitted sweet olives, equal quantity to the capers
ingredients.sourceText: Pitted sweet olives, equal quantity to the capers

steps: Take a handful of capers and press them from vinegar; take as many sweetened olives as, after removing the pit, equal the quantity of capers and chop both finely with a crescent-shaped knife.
Put on the fire a fine mixture of chopped onion with a small piece of butter and when it has taken color, wet it little by little with water so that it breaks down.
Pour into it the mixture of capers and olives and let it boil for a while.
Finally add a drop of vinegar, a pinch of flour and another small piece of butter.
Last add a chopped anchovy, and without letting the sauce boil anymore, serve it.

title: Salsa di Magro per Paste Asciutte (Lean Sauce for Dried Pasta)
description: A sauce made with spaghetti, mushrooms, and pine nuts.

ingredients.name: One quarter of a large onion
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter of a large onion

steps: Place half the butter in a pot and with it brown the pine nuts
Remove the pine nuts dried and pound them in a mortar with the indicated flour
Mince the onion very finely, place it in the remaining sauce and when it has taken on much color, add the tomatoes in pieces
Season with pepper and little salt, and when they are cooked, pass them through a sieve
Return the sauce to the fire with the mushrooms cut into thin slices no larger than a pumpkin seed, the pine nut paste which you can first dissolve with a little water, and the rest of the butter

Bring to a boil for half an hour, adding water to make the sauce more liquid, and lastly dissolve the anchovies on the fire with a little of this sauce, without letting them boil, and combine them with it
Remove the spaghetti dried, season it with this sauce and if you want it better add parmesan cheese
Serves five people

title: Salsa Gialla per Pesce Lesso (Yellow Sauce for Boiled Fish)
description: A sauce made with fish broth, egg yolk, and lemon juice.
steps: Place on the fire in a small pot 20 grams of butter with one heaping teaspoon of flour and after it has taken on a hazelnut color, pour over it little by little two ladles of broth from the fish itself
When you see that the flour, while boiling, no longer rises, remove the sauce from the fire and pour into it two spoonfuls of oil and one egg yolk, stirring well
Finally add the juice of half a lemon, salt and pepper in good measure
Let it cool and then pour it over the fish which you will send to the table surrounded by fresh parsley
This sauce should have the appearance of a cream not too liquid to remain attached to the fish
You will find it is good and delicate
For those who do not like cold fish serve it hot

title: Salsa Maionese (Mayonnaise Sauce)
description: A sauce made with egg yolks, olive oil, and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: Two raw and fresh egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: Two raw and fresh egg yolks

ingredients.name: Olive oil, six or seven spoonfuls or more if absorbed
ingredients.sourceText: Olive oil, six or seven spoonfuls or more if absorbed

steps: Place two raw and fresh egg yolks in a bowl and after whisking them somewhat, let fall on them little by little and almost drop by drop, especially at first, six or seven spoonfuls or even more if they absorb it, of olive oil
Then have them absorb the juice of one lemon
If the sauce turns out well it should have the appearance of a dense cream; but it is necessary to work it for more than 20 minutes
Finally season it with salt and white pepper in good measure
To be more certain of the result, to the two raw egg yolks it is customary to add another hard-boiled one

title: Salsa Tartufata (Truffle Sauce)
description: A sauce made with onion, white wine, and broth.

ingredients.name: Marsala or white wine, two fingers worth
ingredients.sourceText: Marsala or white wine, two fingers worth

steps: Make a very fine mixture with a piece of onion the size of a walnut, half a clove of garlic and a little parsley.
Put it on the fire with 20 grams of butter and when it has taken color pour in two fingers of marsala or white wine in which you have first dissolved a heaping teaspoon of flour.
Season the sauce with a pinch of salt, a pinch of pepper and a pinch of spices and stir it always with a spoon.
When the flour has thickened, add a little broth and then throw very thin slices of truffles into this sauce.
Let it stay another moment on the fire and use it to garnish fried veal cutlets, steaks or other roasted meat.
I warn you that wine, as a condiment, does not suit all stomachs.

If instead of sausage it is cured meat, add a small piece of butter and pour the eggs in after beating them separately

title: Sarde Ripiene (Stuffed Sardines)
description: Prepared with sardines, bread, and anchovies.
steps: Wash the sardines, remove the head, and open them from the belly using your fingers to extract the spine.
Soak the bread crumb in milk and then squeeze it out.
Clean the anchovies of their scales and spine, then chop them.
Mix together the bread crumb, anchovies, egg yolk, half a clove of garlic, and a pinch of oregano, using the blade of a knife to make the mixture fine.
Spread this mixture onto the sardines and close them.
Dip them one by one into the remaining beaten egg white, coat them with breadcrumbs, and fry them in oil.
Salt them lightly and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Sauer-kraut II
description: Prepared with cabbage, onion, and meat.

ingredients.name: Head of cabbage or savoy cabbage
ingredients.sourceText: Head of cabbage or savoy cabbage

steps: Take a head of cabbage or savoy cabbage, cut it into strips about one centimeter wide and keep it soaked in fresh water.
Remove it from the water without squeezing it and press it in a pot over the fire to release its water, which you will then drain by squeezing it with a spoon.

Make a mixture with a quarter of a large onion, some finely chopped cured meat, and a piece of butter; when it takes color, add the said cabbage with a piece of whole cured meat in the middle, which you will remove later, and season with salt and pepper.
Let it boil slowly, moistening it with broth to cook it through and finally add a little vinegar and a teaspoon of sugar, but in such a way that the vinegar is barely noticeable.

title: Savarin (French Ring Cake)
description: A cake made with sweet almonds, beer, and flour.

ingredients.name: Hungarian flour or finest flour, 180 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Hungarian flour or finest flour, 180 grams

ingredients.name: Beer yeast, about the size of a small egg
ingredients.sourceText: Beer yeast, about the size of a small egg

steps: Grease the mold with cold butter, dust it with common flour mixed with powdered sugar, and scatter in the bottom the said almonds, peeled and cut into short strips. If you toast them, you will do better.
Mix and knead the yeast with a drop of the said lukewarm milk and a good pinch of Hungarian flour to make a small dough, which you will allow to rise like the Babà in recipe N. 565.

Put the remaining flour and the other ingredients, except for the milk which is to be added little by little, in a bowl, and begin to work them with a spoon; then add the yeast, and when the mixture is worked so that it detaches well from the bowl, pour it into the mold over the almonds.
Now allow it to rise in a barely warm place, well protected from air, noting that for this second rising you will need four or five hours. Bake it in a common oven or a country oven.

In the meantime prepare the following mixture: boil 30 grams of sugar in two fingers' depth of water in a glass, and when you have reduced it to dense syrup, remove it from the fire and, once cooled, add a teaspoon of vanilla sugar and two tablespoons of rum or kirsch.
Then turn out the savarin and, while still hot, brush it all over with this syrup using a brush until you have used it all. Serve the cake hot or cold as you prefer.
This amount, though small, can serve five or six people. If you see that the dough becomes too liquid with the entire amount of milk, leave some of it aside. It can also be made without the almonds.

title: Scaloppe di Lingua Farsite in Bella Vista (Stuffed Tongue Cutlets in Fine Presentation)
description: Prepared with tongue, ham, and truffle.

ingredients.name: 10 slices of cured tongue from the thickest part, totaling about 130 grams
ingredients.sourceText: 10 slices of cured tongue from the thickest part, totaling about 130 grams

ingredients.name: cooked ham, fat and lean
ingredients.sourceText: 100 grams of cooked ham, fat and lean

steps: Have your charcutier cut ten thin slices of cured tongue from the thickest part, totaling about 130 grams in weight.
Also have cut into thin slices 100 grams of cooked ham, both fat and lean portions.
Trim the edges of the tongue slices all around to give them an elegant shape and set the trimmings aside.
From the ham, cut out ten slices the same size as those of tongue, and put the trimmings of both the ham and tongue into the mortar with {{source-2}} and 20 grams of a white fragrant truffle.
Pound these things together to reduce them fine as an ointment, which you will use to spread on one side of the tongue slices, and stick the ham slices on top.
Now that you have composed these ten pieces, you can take as long as you need to coat them with gelatin (recipe No. 3).

There are two ways to decorate these pieces with the gelatin. The first consists in taking a wide plate or pan, pouring a light layer of melted gelatin, and when it begins to set, placing the pieces on it and covering them with another layer of melted gelatin, then removing them one by one after it has set.

The second way would be to place the pieces upright in a mold at some distance from each other after pouring a light layer of melted gelatin on the bottom, cover them all with the same gelatin, then unmold and send them to the table all in one piece, which will make a finer appearance.
For a meal of several courses this dose could serve ten people, but to be safe it is better not to serve it to more than eight.

title: Scaloppine alla Genovese (Genoese-Style Thin Breaded Veal Cutlets)
description: Prepared with veal, onion, and garlic.

ingredients.name: lean veal meat, 500 grams without bone
ingredients.sourceText: lean veal meat, 500 grams without bone

ingredients.name: one quarter of a medium-sized onion
ingredients.sourceText: one quarter of a medium-sized onion

steps: Form small braised rolls with lean veal meat, and having 500 grams without bone, mince one quarter of a medium-sized onion and place it at the bottom of a saucepan with oil and a small piece of butter.
Lay the braised rolls on the base, one layer on top of the other, season them with salt and pepper and place them on the fire without touching them so that by sticking together they do not shrivel.

When the underside has taken on color, sprinkle a teaspoon of flour and after a little while a pinch of chopped parsley and half a clove of chopped garlic and two sparse fingers of a glass of good white wine, or if lacking this, Marsala.
Then separate the braised rolls from one another, mix, let them draw moisture, then pour hot water and a little tomato juice or preserve.

Let them boil slowly and not for very long to finish cooking them and serve them with abundant sauce, and with slices of toasted bread underneath, or if you prefer, with a side of rice cooked in water, drawn dry and lightly seasoned with butter, Parmesan and the same sauce. Indeed, the rice works very well with this and thus it pleases everyone.

title: Scannello Annegato (Drowned Beef Shank)
description: Prepared with beef or veal, ham, and carrot.

ingredients.name: lean beef or veal without bone from the shank
ingredients.sourceText: 800 grams lean beef or veal without bone from the shank

ingredients.name: 3 or 4 celery ribs about a palm's length
ingredients.sourceText: 3 or 4 celery ribs about a palm's length

ingredients.name: half a glass of dry white wine, or if lacking, two fingers of marsala
ingredients.sourceText: half a glass of dry white wine, or if lacking, two fingers of marsala

steps: Lard the meat with the ham fat cut into strips rolled in salt and pepper
Salt and tie the meat so it stays together
Cut the carrot and celery into small pieces and place them on the bottom of a rather small pot
Place the meat on top and cover with water
Let it boil slowly with the pot covered
When it has reabsorbed the water, strain the sauce and vegetables through a sieve
Return the sauce and vegetables to the fire together with the meat and wine
When cooked, serve it sliced with its sauce on top
This dish can serve six people

title: Sedani per Contorno (Celery as a Side Dish)
description: Prepared with celery, meat stock, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Select celery with full ribs and use only the white ribs and tender stems
Cut into 10 centimeter pieces (or 5 centimeters for the fried version)
After peeling the stem, cut it crosswise and keep it attached to the rib
Boil in salted water for no more than five minutes and remove, draining well
For the first preparation: sauté in butter, finish cooking with meat stock, and add Parmesan cheese when serving

For the second preparation: place 30 grams butter and a battuto made with 30 grams of prosciutto (fat and lean mixed together) and a quarter of a medium onion in a saucepan with two cloves; bring to a boil; when the onion colors, add broth and finish cooking the soffritto; pass everything through a sieve and place the sauce in a pan with the celery pieces; season with pepper (salt is not needed) and serve with the sauce

For the third preparation: flour the celery, dip in batter (recipe N. 156) and fry in lard or oil; or better yet, after flouring, dip in egg, bread it, and fry; this last preparation works better as a side dish to braised meat dishes, which you can use to moisten it

title: Semolino di Magro (Semolina Lean Style)
description: Prepared with semolina, tomato or juice, and egg yolk.

ingredients.name: A piece of butter proportioned to the quantity of semolina
ingredients.sourceText: A piece of butter proportioned to the quantity of semolina

ingredients.name: Two or three eggs mixed with grated Parmesan cheese
ingredients.sourceText: Two or three eggs mixed with grated Parmesan cheese

ingredients.name: For one person: one egg yolk with two tablespoons of Parmesan
ingredients.sourceText: For one person: one egg yolk with two tablespoons of Parmesan

steps: Cook the semolina in water and before removing it from the fire, salt it, dissolve in it a piece of butter proportioned to the quantity of semolina and flavor it with a little tomato juice or conserve.
Beat in the tureen two or three eggs mixed with grated Parmesan and pour the semolina into it.
If it is a soup for only one person, one egg yolk with two tablespoons of Parmesan may be enough.

title: Sformato di Carciofi (Artichoke Molded Dish)
description: Prepared with artichokes, béchamel, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Remove the hardest leaves from the artichokes, trim the tips and peel the stems, keeping them all, even if they are long
Cut them into four wedges and boil them in salted water for only five minutes
Remove them dry, pound them in a mortar and pass them through a sieve

Measure the pulp thus obtained with all those usual ingredients in other vegetable molded dishes, that is: eggs, not being stingy of one more to make it set, two or three spoonfuls of béchamel where butter does not lack, parmesan cheese, salt and the aroma of nutmeg, but taste the mixture several times to bring it to the right flavor
If you have meat broth or stracotto broth, it is not bad to add a little of this too, and if the artichokes are tender, instead of passing them you can leave them in small wedges
Cook it in a water bath in a perforated mold if you have a meat sauce to fill it with; if not, put it in a smooth mold and serve it as a course between other dishes

title: Sformato di cavolfiore (Cauliflower Soufflé)
description: Prepared with cauliflower, parmesan cheese, and milk.
steps: Boil the head of cauliflower halfway in water and then cut it into small pieces
Sauté them with half of the butter, salting them, and when they have absorbed the fat, finish cooking them with a little of the milk; you can then leave them as is or pass them through a sieve
With the remaining butter and milk and one tablespoon of flour make a béchamel and add it to the mixture together with the eggs, first whisked, and the Parmesan
Cook it in a smooth mold like the green bean soufflé and serve it hot
This quantity is enough for six people

title: Sformato di fagiuolini (Green Bean Soufflé)
description: Prepared with green beans, meat or sauce or oil or shallot or parsley or celery, and parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: meat sauce or oil, shallot, parsley, celery
ingredients.sourceText: meat sauce or oil, shallot, parsley, celery

steps: Remove the ends and string from the green beans
Throw them into boiling water with a pinch of salt and as soon as they return to a boil, drain them and throw them into fresh water

If you have meat sauce, season them with this and butter; if not, make a soffritto with a quarter shallot, some parsley leaves, a piece of celery and oil, and when the shallot takes color, throw in the green beans, seasoning with salt and pepper and cooking them with a little water if necessary
Prepare a béchamel with 30 grams of butter, one scant tablespoon of flour and two deciliters of milk
With this, with a handful of grated Parmesan and four whisked eggs, bind the green beans, already cooled
Mix and pour the mixture into a smooth mold, first buttered and whose bottom is covered with a sheet
Cook it over heat or in a bain-marie and serve it hot

title: Sformato di Funghi (Mushroom Mold)
description: Prepared with mushrooms, meat stock, and béchamel.
steps: Clean the mushrooms well from soil and wash them, then chop them finely to the size of a chickpea or less.
Put them on the fire with butter, salt and pepper and when they have softened somewhat, cook them through with meat stock.
Remove from fire, bind them with béchamel, eggs and parmigiano and set the mixture in a bain-marie.
600 grams of mushrooms in nature with five eggs will make a mold sufficient for ten people.
Serve it hot and as an intermediate course.

title: Sformato di Zucchini Passati (Zucchini Mold)
description: Prepared with zucchini, onion, and celery.
steps: Make a battuto with a quarter onion, celery, carrot and parsley.
Put it on the fire with oil and when it takes color pour in the zucchini cut into small pieces seasoned with salt and pepper.
When they are browned, cook them through with water, pass them dry through the sieve and add the parmigiano and eggs.
Make a béchamel with 60 grams of butter, two tablespoons of flour and 4 deciliters of milk.
Mix everything together and, using a smooth perforated mold, cook it in a bain-marie.
Unmold it hot, fill the center with a delicate sauce and serve it.
This amount will serve eight or ten people.

title: Soufflet di Luisetta (Luisetta's Soufflé)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, milk, and sugar.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them and pound them very fine with a spoonful of the said sugar.

Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk poured hot. Before removing it from the fire add the almonds, the sugar and the flavour. Once it is cooled, combine with the eggs, first the yolks and then the beaten whites.
Butter a baking pan that can withstand heat, pour the mixture into it and finish cooking it in a country-style oven.
This will be sufficient for five or six people.

title: Soufflé di Farina di Patate (Potato Starch Soufflé)
description: Prepared with potato starch, vanilla or lemon zest, and sugar.

ingredients.name: Eggs, 3 whole eggs plus 2 or 3 extra whites
ingredients.sourceText: Eggs, 3 whole eggs plus 2 or 3 extra whites

steps: Place the sugar and flour in a saucepan and pour in the cold milk little by little, stirring
Set the mixture on the fire so it thickens, stirring constantly, without worrying about making it boil
Add the vanilla or lemon zest, and when it becomes lukewarm, mix in the 3 egg yolks, then whip the whites and fold them in gently
Pour it into a metal baking dish and place it on the stovetop, cover it with the lid of a country oven between two fires and wait for it to puff up and brown lightly
Then dust it with powdered sugar and send it immediately to the table, where it will be praised for its delicacy; if any remains, you will find it is also good cold

title: Spaghetti alla Rustica (Rustic Spaghetti)
description: Prepared with tomatoes, spaghetti or vermicelli, and parmesan cheese.
steps: Make a small mixture with two cloves of garlic and a good pinch of parsley and the aroma of basil if desired; put it in a pan with a good amount of oil.
As soon as the garlic begins to color, add six or seven tomatoes cut into pieces, seasoning them with salt and pepper.
When well cooked, pass the sauce through a strainer.
Dress the spaghetti or vermicelli (cooked briefly in plenty of salted water) with the sauce and grated Parmesan cheese.
Send immediately to table so they remain succulent.
Tagliatelle can also be seasoned this way.

title: Spaghetti coi Naselli (Spaghetti with Hake)
description: Prepared with spaghetti, hake, and onion.

ingredients.name: Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water
ingredients.sourceText: Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water

steps: Chop a medium-sized onion and squeeze it between your hands to remove its bitterness
Put it on the fire with the oil and when it begins to brown, throw in the hake cut into pieces and season them with salt and pepper
Once browned, pour in tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water to cook them, and then pass them through a wire sieve, wetting them with a little hot water if needed, to extract all the pulp

Put the passed mixture back on the fire with the butter, Marsala, nutmeg and when it has come to a boil, if the sauce does not need to be reduced to the right consistency, dress the spaghetti cooked in salted water with this sauce and Parmesan
This is a portion for five people and is a pasta course that will please because it is not a jumble as the description might suggest

title: Spaghetti col Sugo di Seppie (Spaghetti with Cuttlefish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with spaghetti, bread, and onion.

ingredients.name: tomato juice or conserve in large quantity
ingredients.sourceText: tomato juice or conserve in large quantity

steps: Skin and clean the cuttlefish by removing the bone, mouth apparatus, eyes, digestive tube, and ink sac.

Make a mixture with 100 grams bread crumb, a good pinch of parsley and one clove of garlic, add the tentacles (two per cuttlefish) finely chopped, season with oil, salt and pepper, and use this to fill the cuttlefish sac, sewing the mouth closed.
Chop one onion of medium size, squeeze it to remove bitterness and put it in a pan with oil over heat; when it takes color, add the cuttlefish and season with salt and pepper.
Wait until they color, then cook them slowly with much tomato juice or conserve, adding water gradually.
Boil for three hours, ensuring enough sauce remains to season the pasta.
Season 500 grams of spaghetti with the sauce and grated Parmesan cheese.
Serve the cuttlefish afterwards as a fish course in sauce.

title: Spaghetti colle Acciughe (Spaghetti with Anchovies)
description: Prepared with spaghetti, anchovies, and tomato or juice.

description: Prepared with yeast, orange, and eggs.
steps: Mix the two kinds of wine and infuse the anise in a little of this liquid after washing them well

title: Stiacciata coi Siccioli (Flatbread with Cracklings)
description: Prepared with bread, powdered sugar, and lard.

ingredients.name: Scent of orange or lemon zest
ingredients.sourceText: Scent of orange or lemon zest

steps: Prepare it the evening before; first work the yeast on the work surface without the seasonings, then in a bowl for more than half an hour by hand, adding the ingredients and eggs gradually
Cover well and place in a warm location so it rises during the night
The following morning remix it and pour it into a buttered and floured copper baking pan where it should be no more than two fingers thick
Send it to the warm chamber for the second rising and pass it to the oven
You can also complete the entire operation at home and cook it in a countryside oven, but be warned this is a somewhat difficult dough to succeed with, especially if the season is very cold
It is better to make it when the weather is mild, but do not be discouraged at the first attempt
If in the morning it has risen little or not at all, add baker's yeast in a quantity slightly more than a walnut, letting it first rise separately with a pinch of flour and lukewarm water

title: Stiacciate alla Livornese (Livornese Flatbread)
description: Prepared with yeast, wine, and orange flower water.
steps: Dissolve the brewer's yeast with half a glass of lukewarm water, adding enough flour to form a dough of proper consistency, which you will place on the mound of flour within a bowl, covering it with a layer of the same flour. Keep the bowl protected from air and in the kitchen, or in the warmest place in your house if you have one.

In the morning, when the said dough has risen well, place it on the work surface, flatten it and remix it with one egg, one tablespoon of oil, one of sugar, one of wine and enough flour to form once again a larger dough, mixing everything well without working it too much. Replace it on the flour and cover it as before.

After six or seven hours, which will be needed for the dough to rise again, add three eggs, three tablespoons of oil, three of sugar, three of wine, and enough flour to form the usual dough and let it rise again, proceeding always in the same manner. To know the point of fermentation, calculate that the dough must increase about three times in volume.
Add five eggs, five tablespoons of sugar, five of oil, five of wine and the necessary flour.

Add the three remaining eggs and everything else, melting the butter over heat, and mix very well to make the dough homogeneous. If the dough becomes somewhat soft, which is unlikely, add more flour to bring it to the proper consistency.

Divide it into three or four parts forming balls and place each one in a baking pan on a sheet of paper that extends beyond the rim, greased with butter, where it lies flat; and since as the dose of ingredients increases, fermentation is slower, the last time, if you wish to hasten it, place the flatbreads to rise in a warm place and when they are well puffed and trembling, brush them with a brush first dipped in orange flower water, then in egg yolk. Bake them in the oven at a very moderate temperature, noting that this last part is the most important and difficult because, being large in volume, there is the chance that strong heat reaches the surface immediately, and the interior remains soft.

title: Storni in istufato (Stewed Starlings)
description: Prepared with onion, lard, and berries.

ingredients.name: One quarter of a large onion
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter of a large onion

ingredients.name: Three or four strips of fatty and lean prosciutto
ingredients.sourceText: Three or four strips of fatty and lean prosciutto

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or marsala and water
ingredients.sourceText: Dry white wine or marsala and water

steps: Make a fine battuto (chopped mixture) with a quarter of a large onion and 30 grams of lard fat.
Heat this in a pot with 20 grams of butter, three or four strips of prosciutto, and 2 juniper berries.
Place the starlings on top without gutting them, garnish with sage leaves, and season with salt and pepper.
Turn them often until they absorb the flavors and the onion is well colored.

Moisten with a little dry white wine, then add enough wine (or a mixture of water and marsala) so that the total liquid added is three deciliters, or if lacking white wine, use two deciliters water and one of marsala.
Cover the pot with a sheet of paper folded four times, held down by a heavy lid, and simmer gently until completely cooked.
Serve the birds with their sauce.

title: Stracotto alla Bizzarra (Bizarrely Braised Veal)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and garlic.

ingredients.name: Lean veal without bone, 700 to 800 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Lean veal without bone, 700 to 800 grams

ingredients.name: Marsala wine, one finger measure of a glass
ingredients.sourceText: Marsala wine, one finger measure of a glass

steps: Lard the veal with pieces of lard the thickness of a finger, which you will have first seasoned with salt and pepper, and season the meat the same way.
Tie it so it stays compact and place it in a pot half covered with water with two sage leaves, a bunch of rosemary and half a garlic clove; if the meat is very tender use less water.
When, in boiling, it has become dry, let it take on color with a teaspoon of flour.
Add a piece of butter, then wet it with a ladle of broth and a finger measure of a glass of marsala.
Strain the sauce without squeezing it and pour it over the piece of meat when you serve it at table.

title: Stracotto alla Fiorentina (Florentine Braised Veal)
description: Prepared with veal, meat, and onion.

ingredients.name: Lean veal with bone or joint, 500 grams
ingredients.sourceText: Lean veal with bone or joint, 500 grams

ingredients.name: One quarter of a large onion
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter of a large onion

steps: Chop the onion, carrot, and celery coarsely and cut the cured meat into small dice.
Put everything together in a pot and season with salt and pepper.
Turn the meat frequently and when it is browned, sprinkle a pinch of flour over it.
Pour tomato juice or paste over it and cook it through with water added little by little.
The flour serves to bind the sauce and give it color, but be careful that it does not burn or it will give an unpleasant taste and a nearly black color which the sauce should not have.
Strain the sauce, and if desired, add aroma with a few pieces of dried mushrooms, first softened in hot water and boiled a little in the sauce.
Cook the macaroni in salted water and drain well, then keep it briefly in the sauce near the fire and season with butter and a modest amount of parmesan cheese, as this can be added at table.

title: Strichetti alla Bolognese (Bolognese Pasta Knots)
description: Prepared with broth, flour, and eggs.
steps: Mix the flour with two eggs, 40 grams of finely grated Parmesan and the flavor of nutmeg
Pull out a sheet not too thin and cut it with the fluted wheel into so many strips wide a finger and a half
Then, with the same wheel, cut these strips diagonally and at the same distance of a finger and a half to make so many pieces in the shape of an almond
Take them one at a time and squeeze with your fingers the four points, two above and two below to form as it were two little rings attached together
Cook them in broth with little cooking
The dose of two eggs will be sufficient for five people

title: Strudel (Apple Strudel)
description: Prepared with apples, currants, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: reinette apples or tender apples of good quality
ingredients.sourceText: 500 grams reinette apples or tender apples of good quality

ingredients.name: two or three pinches of ground cinnamon
ingredients.sourceText: two or three pinches of ground cinnamon

steps: Mix the flour with hot milk, a nut-sized piece of butter, one egg and a pinch of salt to make a rather firm dough and let it rest a little before using it.
Roll out with this dough a thin sheet like that of taglierini and, leaving the edges uncovered, spread the apples on top, which you will have first peeled, cleaned of cores and cut into thin slices.
On the layer of apples scatter the currants, the lemon zest, the cinnamon, the sugar and finally the 100 grams of melted butter, leaving a little aside for later use.

Once done, wrap the sheet over itself to form a filled roll and fit it into a buttered copper pan, accommodating the rounded shape as necessary; with the remaining butter grease the entire outer part of the pastry and send it to the oven.

Note that currants, or sultana raisins, are different from raisins. The latter are small and black; the former are twice as large, light chestnut in color and also without seeds. Scrape the lemon with a piece of glass.

title: Sugo di carne (Meat Gravy)
description: A sauce made with lard or meat, onion, and carrot.

ingredients.name: Thin slices of lard or cured meat (the latter is preferable)
ingredients.sourceText: Thin slices of lard or cured meat (the latter is preferable)

ingredients.name: Lean beef meat in pieces or thin slices
ingredients.sourceText: Lean beef meat in pieces or thin slices

ingredients.name: Small ladle of cold water (repeated three times)
ingredients.sourceText: Small ladle of cold water (repeated three times)

ingredients.name: hot water or broth made from spongy bones (for approximately 500 grams of meat)
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 liters hot water or broth made from spongy bones (for approximately 500 grams of meat)

steps: Cover the bottom of a pot with thin slices of lard or cured meat
Above these, slice a large onion, a carrot, and a celery rib
Add here and there small pieces of butter and above these ingredients spread lean beef meat in pieces or thin slices
Season with only salt and two cloves
Place the pot over fire without ever touching it
When you smell the odor of burnt onion, turn the meat, and when you see it well browned, indeed almost black, pour cold water from a small ladle
Repeat the operation of pouring water three times as it evaporates
Finally, if the quantity of meat is about 500 grams, pour into the pot 1.5 liters of hot water or preferably a broth made from spongy bones
Let it boil gently for five or six consecutive hours to reduce the gravy and extract all the substance from the meat
Pass it through a strainer and when its fat has congealed, forming a large layer on top, remove it all to make the gravy less heavy on the stomach

steps: From one kilogram of lean beef meat (including bone), take 400 grams cut into thin slices
With the rest, make broth as usual with {{source-2}}
Cover the bottom of a pot with slices of lard and prosciutto and some small pieces of butter
Slice an onion and place the thin slices of beef arranged on top
When the meat has taken on color over high heat from below, wet it with a ladle of the said broth, then turn it so it also colors on the other side, and after pour another ladle of broth
Then season with salt, one clove or nine to ten crushed peppercorns, and one teaspoon of sugar
Pour now all the rest of the broth, add a carrot cut into slices and a decorated bouquet that can be composed of parsley, celery and some other aromatic herb
Boil gently for about two hours, then remove the thin slices of meat, strain the gravy and remove the fat
With this you can wet soup and use it to flavor vegetables, or, thickening it with a mixture of potato flour and butter, dress dry soups

title: Tagliatelle col Prosciutto (Ribbon Pasta with Prosciutto)
description: Prepared with fat, celery, and carrot.

ingredients.name: Eggs and flour for pasta dough, no water

ingredients.name: Broth or water (if using tomato paste)

steps: Cut a thick slice of prosciutto into small dice
Finely chop celery and carrot in quantities such that both together make approximately the volume of the prosciutto
Put these three ingredients on the fire together with a piece of butter proportionate to the amount of pasta
When the mixture has taken on color, add tomato juice or tomato paste, but with paste you need a ladle of broth or water
Make and roll out the pasta dough into a sheet somewhat thicker than thin noodles and cut into wider strips
Cook the tagliatelle briefly and salt them very little because of the prosciutto; remove them dry and season them with the sauce and parmesan cheese

title: Tagliatelle Verdi (Green Ribbon Pasta)
description: Prepared with spinach, eggs, and flour.

ingredients.name: Spinach, cooked and drained, a handful
ingredients.sourceText: Spinach, cooked and drained, a handful

steps: Cook spinach, squeeze it well and chop it with a curved knife
With 2 eggs and a handful of this chopped spinach, mix flour on a work surface to obtain a very firm pasta dough which you will work a lot by hand
With a rolling pin, roll it out to a thin sheet and when it begins to stick because of the herb which produces stickiness, sprinkle it lightly with flour
Wrap the sheet in a cloth and when it is dry cut it somewhat wider than thin noodles for broth, noting that the beauty of such pasta is its length which indicates the skill of who made it
As soon as the water comes to a boil remove the pasta dry and season it as with spaghetti alla rustica, or as with macaroni or tagliatelle, or simply with cheese and butter

description: Prepared with semolina and eggs.
steps: Fine semolina is required and it needs to be soaked with eggs several hours before pulling out the sheet.
If when you are about to pull it out it turns out too soft, add a few pinches of dry semolina to reduce the dough to the necessary hardness so it does not stick to the rolling pin.
No salt or other ingredients are needed.

title: Telline o arselle in salsa d'uovo (Clams or Arkshells in Egg Sauce)
description: A sauce made with clams, garlic, and egg yolks.
steps: Put the clams or arkshells on the fire with a soffritto of garlic, oil, parsley, and a pinch of pepper.
Shake them and keep the vessel covered so they do not dry out.
Remove them when they have opened.
For the sauce, use one or more egg yolks depending on the quantity, lemon juice, one teaspoon of flour, broth, and some of the juice that came out from the clams.
Cook it like a cream and pour it over the clams when you serve them at table.

title: Telline o Arselle in Salsa d'Uovo (Clams or Mussels in Egg Sauce)
description: A sauce made with clams or mussels, garlic, and egg yolks.
steps: Rinse the mussels well in fresh water. Place them in a pot with a soffritto of garlic, oil, parsley and a pinch of pepper, cover and shake the pot so they do not dry out. Remove them when they open and prepare the following sauce: one or more egg yolks depending on quantity, lemon juice, a teaspoon of flour, broth and some of the juice that came from the clams. Cook it like a cream and pour it over the clams when serving. Alternatively, serve without sauce poured over slices of bread dried by the fire.
